docs.title: Jackie-OS
docs.text:
A second brain plus an always-on AI agent, wired together. The vault (Obsidian) is memory; skills (markdown playbooks) are the contract; Hermes (a VPS agent) runs the loop 24/7. You stay CEO; this site explains the rest.

CaptureDM a thought, link, or meeting — it files itself into the vault → Brief07:30 morning brief: what changed, top 3, calendar → Buildworkers (Cyrus, Codex) take Linear issues → PRs → Syncmerges write back to project Status + hot.md → Compoundlearnings, decisions, reviews accrete in the vault The loop — every layer reads and writes the same second brain, so nothing starts cold.

docs.title: 1. What is this system?
docs.text: Start with what Jackie-OS does — the plain-English walkthrough. Then the system map (one page, top to bottom: you → vault/skills → Hermes → workers → back to you) and the vocabulary.

docs.title: 2. What do I do?
docs.text: The cheat-sheet: the ~5 things you say ("wrap up", "grill me", "research X", reviews) — everything else is automatic. Plus: closing a session, fixing the VPS, adding a project.

docs.title: 3. What runs by itself?
docs.text: Every scheduled job on one page — the 07:00–07:30 morning stack, hourly journal, merge-poll, autodeploy — and which project syncs from where.

docs.title: 4. What's the plan?
docs.text:
The roadmap (active plans, shipped ledger), the ideas backlog, and the decisions log — the durable why.

Looking for something specific? Use search (top bar) — every skill, script, and doc is indexed. Or start from the master index.

The one rule: before building anything new, check the master index for prior art. When something ships, its doc updates in the same commit — so this site is always current.

This site renders the repo's markdown directly (docs-site/, symlinked — no copies). Serve: bash System/tools/docs-site.sh serve → 127.0.0.1:8123.

docs.title: Ecosystem Architecture
docs.text:
One operator, three systems, one spine. Jackie-OS is the always-on AI operating layer; Newfin and Rodyna are independent product repos that ride the same shared rails. The spine is Hermes (the VPS gateway): the single LLM gateway, the cron host, and the SSH bridge into Newfin.

Quick rule for agents: code lives in ~/dev/{newfin,rodyna,draw} (CTO territory). Knowledge about the code lives in the vault (Vault/Newfin.md, Vault/Rodyna.md). Technical fix write-ups live in each repo's docs/solutions/. Don't confuse the two.

    FINBOT["@Persik_finbot<br>money bot"]
    HERMESBOT["@persik_hermes_bot<br>COO · CTO agent"]
    subgraph JOS["JACKIE-OS — the AI OS"]
        direction TB
        HERMES["Hermes VPS · Agent SDK<br>cron stack · LLM gateway"]
        SKILLS["Skills + Scripts"]

    end
    NEWFIN["Newfin (~/dev)<br>net-worth + advisor"]
    RODYNA["Rodyna (~/dev)<br>family recipes"]
    RAILS["Shared rails<br>Supabase · Vercel<br>LLM: OAuth subs — Fable 5 / Haiku / Terra"]

Solid = data/control flow · dotted knowledge about = vault notes, not code · Newfin & Rodyna would run without Jackie-OS; Hermes is what makes it one OS.

docs.title: 1. Jackie-OS — the AI operating system
docs.text:
Sergei's always-on OS. The vault is memory, skills are the contract, scripts are dumb runners, Hermes is the 24/7 instance on a VPS. Tool-agnostic: any agent that opens ~/Jackie-OS and reads CLAUDE.md becomes an instance. Hosts four code repos (Newfin, Rodyna, Draw, B-Unit) and multiple products/projects (B-Unit, Peaches Beauty, Nastusha), all synced to the vault via project-sync.

  • Stack: Obsidian (markdown) · bash/Python runners · Claude Agent SDK · VPS cron (Europe/Warsaw) · git + symlink farm · Telegram Bot API.
  • Layers:
  • Vault (Vault/) — journals, project notes, briefs, coaching corpus, ops board, Agent-Learnings/ index. Source of truth.
  • Skills (System/skills/) — markdown agent specs (morning-brief, project-sync, research, wrap-up, coaching, …).
  • Scripts (System/{coo,capture,ops,periodic,work,lib}/) — edited in repo, run on VPS via a symlink farm (~/.hermes/scripts/<name> → repo). Repo is the source of truth; never edit the VPS copy.
    • Script groups by function:
    • coo/ — COO ops (brief delivery, Telegram integration, vault index updates)
    • capture/ — journal capture, Telegram sweep, trade digest, meeting capture
    • ops/ — VPS service health, Hermes ops proxy, code exec gate, notify endpoint
    • periodic/ — intel weekly, codebase index (cbm), janitor maintenance
    • work/ — ad-hoc agent work (code ask, wrap-up ops)
    • lib/ — shared utilities (env loader, logging helpers)
  • Secrets (.secrets/*.env) — gitignored, mode 0600.
  • Hermes VPS (hermes@your-vps-host) — one Agent SDK instance as the hermes user; one LLM gateway for all calls (failover chain). Dashboard :9119, Headroom proxy :8787.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Claude takes a functional role per task. Each role defines what to read and produce:

Role What it does COO (default) Personal assistant / PM. Daily briefs, task lists, project status, calendar, ops board. CPO Planning, feature scoping, roadmap work on project notes. CMO Marketing: SEO/content for Peaches Beauty, community virality. CRO Community research (research <topic>, last30days engine, optional and file → Clippings). CTO Code in ~/dev/{newfin,rodyna,draw} via Claude Code / Cursor. Same agent, different hat. CFO Financial analysis; Newfin/Persik handle live data, vault holds decisions only. Coach Recovery, identity, periodic reviews (week/month/year).

Agent portability: any editor that opens ~/Jackie-OS and reads CLAUDE.md auto-becomes a Jackie-OS agent. Hermes VPS is simply the always-on 24/7 instance of that same agent.

docs.title: Automation reality (2026-07-10)
docs.text:
Three automation layers (a job must never live in multiple, or it double-runs). The VPS owns everything; Cowork on the Mac is effectively retired — one leftover schedule (weekly-review) is all that remains:

Layer Jobs Hermes Agent cron (hermes cron list) morning-brief (07:30) · journal-capture (hourly) · telegram-sweep (07:00) · trade-digest (07:10) — 4 jobs OS crontab (crontab -l, hermes user) autodeploy (*/2) · merge-poll (~2h) · healthcheck (08:00) · degraded-brief (08:35) · intel-weekly (Sun) · cbm-index (Sun) · janitor (quarterly) Mac weekly-review (last Cowork schedule) jackie-os-weekly-review (Sun 18:00) — compound + weekly brief generation

Research is on-demand only. The 06:45 research-bridge agent-cron was removed 2026-06-30 — research runs only via the research <topic> skill, the Persik /research queue, or hermes-ops flush research. Watchlist auto-research no longer runs unattended.

Morning brief flow (07:30): git pull → project-sync (thin merge-poll on VPS) → LLM brief → calendar → Telegram + HTML → single commit + push. Backstop: degraded-brief at 08:35 if no deliverable brief exists.

docs.title: 2. Newfin — net-worth + financial advisor (~/dev/newfin)
docs.text:
Open-source personal-finance platform: net worth across crypto, real estate, equities, cash. API-first (/v1), an LLM advisor, and the household Telegram bot @Persik_finbot. Read-only at the UX layer — monitors Binance futures, never executes trades.

  • Stack: Node 20 + Express (TS, ESM) · React 19 + Vite + Tailwind · Supabase Postgres + RLS · Vercel/VPS · Recharts/React Query/Zustand · Zod.
  • Workspaces:
  • /shared (@newfin/shared) — NW math, FX, scenario engine, Zod schemas.
  • /server — /v1 REST, integrations, lib/advisor, alert-engine, futures-service.
  • /server/persik — bot: dispatch · lanes (Advisor/Journal) · menus · ops-proxy · hermes-bridge · queue-worker.
  • /web — Portfolio, Trading Desk, Cashflow, Advisor, Goals, Integrations.
  • Integrations: Binance Futures · Zerion · CoinGecko · Monobank · EtherFi · exchangerate.host · Telegram · Hermes VPS (ssh) · Claude → Gemini.
  • Key patterns: lane-based bot routing; Hermes bridge SSH-forwards owner advisor turns to the VPS; 24h-cached LLM context (hash of state+intel+memory); role-scoped views (scopeForViewer); fill-driven futures position reconstruction + income-ledger enrichment; structured (Zod) LLM output.
  • Advisor flow: TG webhook → role+lane → assemble FinancialState → LLM (24h cache) → reply + thread.
  • Deeper: repo docs/, Vault/Newfin.md.

docs.title: 3. Rodyna — family recipes (~/dev/rodyna)
docs.text:
Telegram-first family recipe app: captures recipes (YouTube / photo / text) with their stories and bilingual (EN + UK) context, extracts ingredients + nutrition via AI, then does weekly meal planning + grocery lists. Multi-tenant by design ("family now, product later"); ~$0/mo on free tiers.

  • Stack: Supabase Edge Functions (Deno) · grammY bot framework · Supabase Postgres + RLS + Storage · React 18 + Vite (Telegram Mini App) · Vercel · Zod · @rodyna/ui.
  • Modules:
  • telegram-webhook — entry point, acks <1s, enqueues a jobs row.
  • process-recipe — async worker: Gemini extract → ingredient catalog → USDA nutrition → persist.
  • api — REST for the Mini App (auth via Telegram initData, CRUD, search).
  • _shared/worker + packages/shared — gemini, usda, catalog, prompts, i18n.
  • Integrations: Telegram · Google Gemini (flash/flash-lite) · USDA FoodData Central · Supabase Cloud · Vercel.
  • Key patterns: async job queue (fast-ack via waitUntil, idempotent, pg_cron sweep retry); immutable originals (DB trigger blocks edits) + full version snapshots; Zod at every boundary; ingredient-catalog specificity matching.
  • Ingest flow: YouTube link → ack + jobs row → Gemini extract → USDA + Nutri-Score → edit message into a recipe card.
  • Deeper: repo docs/02-ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/03-DATA-MODEL.md, Vault/Rodyna.md.

docs.title: 4. Draw — tennis community platform (~/dev/draw)
docs.text:
Shared dev environment for the Draw platform: tournaments (registration, NTRP gating, single elim / round robin / Swiss draws, scoring, standings), seasonal leagues, challenge matches, casual games, rankings, notifications. Delivered as Telegram Mini App + web app + native mobile sharing one Next.js backend.

  • Stack: Next.js App Router (apps/web/) · React Native CLI (apps/mobile/) · Supabase Postgres · packages/shared (domain logic, draw algorithms, i18n) · FastAPI sidecar (services/auto_post/) for cross-platform reel publishing · next-intl (en/ru/uk/pl/be) · Web Push (VAPID) + APNS · Sentry.
  • Status: Active dev environment. Not yet in production. Morning-brief merge-poll skips Draw (read-only watcher).
  • Deeper: repo ARCHITECTURE.md, docs/, Vault/Draw.md.

docs.title: 4b. B-Unit — habit + quest app (~/dev/bunit + Projects/B-Unit/)
docs.text:
Product in active development: economy model (quests, rewards, real-money cashout, habit tracking), coached XP progression, Telegram entry point. Pilot vanguard user (Bim) on live prod.

  • Stack: Supabase (Postgres, edge functions), Next.js, Telegram bot, coaching loop, pgTAP tests.
  • Tracking: First project on Linear (evegelin workspace, B-Unit project + B-Unit — Content for TikTok episode production). Task state syncs on ship per ~/dev/bunit/docs/linear-workflow.md § Sync contract, and back into project-sync/morning-brief via the registry tracker: linear flag (System/scripts/linear-fetch.py). Two autonomous agents live (Claude Code / Cyrus on Hermes + ChatGPT Codex in CI) — agents dispatch from backlog → PR flow auto-synced to Linear.
  • Deployment: One-click migration + deploy button; migrations/00NN.sql + E2E verification script before prod apply.
  • Key recent (2026-07-07): economy-integrity fixes (0024–0025), timer verification flow change, equipment equip/unequip, theme picker; all migrations applied to prod + verified live.
  • Deeper: repo docs/linear-workflow.md (sync contract), Vault/B-Unit.md.

docs.title: 5. Shared rails — same infra, different products
docs.text:
Layer Jackie-OS Newfin Rodyna Draw B-Unit Front door @persik_hermes_bot + Cursor/Claude Code @Persik_finbot + React web app Telegram bot + React Mini App @persik_hermes_bot (read-only poll, no push) Telegram bot + web shell Runtime Claude Agent SDK on VPS + bash/python Node 20 + Express (TS) Supabase Edge Functions (Deno) Next.js App Router + React Native Supabase Edge Functions + Next.js + Telegram Data store Obsidian vault (markdown + git) Supabase Postgres + RLS Supabase Postgres + RLS + Storage Supabase Postgres + RLS Supabase Postgres + RLS Hosting VPS (hermes user) Vercel / VPS Vercel (Mini App) + Supabase Cloud Vercel (web) + local dev (mobile) Vercel + Supabase Cloud Intelligence One Hermes gateway · Claude → Gemini Claude → Gemini, 24h cache Gemini flash / flash-lite Claude / Gemini (planned) Claude (advisor) / Gemini (AI extraction) Validation Skill frontmatter + review Zod at trust boundaries Zod at trust boundaries Zod at trust boundaries Zod at trust boundaries · pgTAP migrations Writes Git commits (human + agent) Vercel deploys Supabase deploys Vercel deploys; vault is read-only watcher Supabase Edge Fn + migrations; Cyrus/Codex auto-dispatch Tracking Vault (roadmap-index.md + future-improvements.md) Vault (roadmap-index.md + future-improvements.md) Vault (roadmap-index.md + future-improvements.md) Vault (read-only) Linear (B-Unit project, workspace EVE)

The spine is Hermes. Newfin and Rodyna are fully independent repos with their own Supabase projects and deploys — they'd run without Jackie-OS. What ties the ecosystem together: Hermes owns the morning/journal cron, is the single LLM gateway (Claude → Gemini failover), and SSH-bridges Newfin's owner advisor turns. The vault never holds code — only knowledge about the repos; each repo's docs/solutions/ holds the technical learnings, indexed back into Vault/Agent-Learnings/.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: Shared domain vocabulary for this project — entities, named processes, and status concepts with project-specific meaning. Seeded with core domain vocabulary, then accretes as ce-compound and ce-compound-refresh process learnings; direct edits are fine. Glossary only, not a spec or catch-all.

docs.title: Core terms — used daily
docs.text:
• hot.md — A ~500-word cache in Vault/hot.md of current focus and open loops, refreshed at every session end; fastest orientation for any agent starting a new session.
  • wrap-up — The wrap-up skill (System/skills/wrap-up/SKILL.md) that syncs the vault, updates ## Status in project notes, refreshes hot.md, and commits.
  • brief — An AI-generated daily or period summary (morning brief, weekly brief) that reads code activity, vault status, and calendar to inform the day.
  • skill — A repeatable workflow playbook (markdown + optional code) living in System/skills/; an AI reads it and executes the defined steps. Global owned skills carry the jos- prefix (see System/SKILLS.md § Naming).
  • Hermes — The always-on VPS agent (hermes@your-vps-host) that runs the scheduled tasks and sync loop while your Mac is off.
  • Persik — Two Telegram bots: @Persik_finbot (the Newfin-hosted product bot) and @persik_hermes_bot (the full Hermes VPS channel).
  • workers — Autonomous agents building from Linear: Cyrus (Claude Code on the VPS) and Codex (ChatGPT in GitHub CI). See § Linear integration below.
  • registry — The System/project-registry.md file that maps each project to its code repo and/or STATUS file, serving as the single source of truth for sync.

docs.title: Occasional
docs.text:
• janitor — An OKF linter and maintenance tool that audits frontmatter compliance and keeps the vault structure clean (quarterly cron).
  • docs-first — Before building anything new, check DOCS.md (master index) for prior art; on ship, update the owning doc in the same commit.

docs.title: Deprecated / winding down
docs.text:
• Cowork — The Claude desktop app's scheduled-tasks harness on Sergei's Mac. Effectively retired — a single leftover schedule remains (Sunday 18:00 weekly-review); everything else runs on the VPS.
  • Bases/Ops board — Obsidian Bases kanban for task tracking. Being replaced by Linear (migration in progress: B-Unit, Newfin, Rodyna already on Linear; Jackie-OS itself deliberately stays on Bases/markdown).

docs.title: Jackie OS agent (any editor; Hermes optional)
docs.text: Jackie OS is portable files — the vault, the skills, the rules. Any AI coding tool that opens the ~/Jackie-OS folder (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) auto-reads CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and runs the skills that live inside it, becoming a Jackie OS agent; the skills aren't moved or copied — a few cross-project ones (e.g. wrap up) are installed once in ~/.agents/skills/. wrap up from any editor syncs the vault, ## Status, and hot.md, then commits. Hermes (below) is simply the always-on instance of that same agent on the VPS — it runs the schedule unattended. Hermes is not required to use the system; it only automates the loop.

docs.title: OKF (Open Knowledge Format) bundle
docs.text: Jackie-OS adopts Open Knowledge Format frontmatter — every skill, solution, concept, project note, daily, and brief carries structured YAML (type, title, timestamp, …). This makes the vault a portable, vendor-neutral knowledge bundle: anyone can fork the structure and wire a different automation layer, and any agent can orient and retrieve by metadata instead of inferring from prose. Frontmatter only — internal links stay as Obsidian wikilinks (OKF's relative-link convention is not adopted). Backfilled by System/tools/add-okf-frontmatter.py; enforced by janitor OKF lint mode. Headline goal = portability; faster agent orientation/retrieval is the day-to-day payoff.

docs.title: Hermes VPS
docs.text:
The VPS worker layer (hermes@your-vps-host) — runs the Hermes agent (hermes-gateway), crons, and the ops exec allowlist. Models run on subscription OAuth CLIs, not API-price billing (Nous Portal credits exhausted 2026-07-06; owner opted out of API pricing). Two Hermes profiles (as of 2026-07-10):

Profile Model Auth Used for default (live gateway) claude-fable-5 @ high effort → claude-haiku-4.5 → gpt-5.6-terra Claude sub OAuth token; Codex CLI OAuth for Terra briefs, journal, cron ops, @persik_hermes_bot persiknewfin gpt-5.6-terra @ xhigh effort → gpt-oss-120b:free (OpenRouter) → gemini-2.5-flash Codex CLI OAuth; OpenRouter + Gemini API keys manual/gateway agentic runs (web + terminal toolsets, verify-on-stop)

Auxiliary roles (vision, web-extract, compression, title generation, delegation subagents, …) run gpt-5.4-mini (Codex CLI OAuth) with claude-haiku-4.5 fallback.

Newfin's /ask + /research shell the subscription OAuth CLIs directly (Claude Code / Codex), not a Hermes profile. Voice/photo STT stays direct-Gemini with Newfin's own key×model failover (gemini-media-chain, fallback gemini-3.5-flash). Source: newfin plans/decisions-log.md 2026-07-06 + 2026-07-04.

docs.title: Two-bot model
docs.text:
Two live Telegram bots, split by audience:

  • @Persik_finbot — the Newfin-hosted Telegram product bot: money COO, /day, /week, spouse-scoped routes, and owner ops (status, sync vault). Credentials stay on Vercel; never deployed to the Hermes VPS. /ask and /research run subscription OAuth CLIs directly (Claude Code / Codex — not a Hermes profile, since 2026-07-06). /research routes through the Persik counsel lane as an agentic, web-searching research turn (web toolset) that relates findings to the owner's book only when they connect; live_market keeps a synchronous Binance price path. /scout + /deep-research were folded into /research (2026-06-30).
  • @persik_hermes_bot — the full Telegram channel for the Hermes VPS agent: COO, CTO, journal, crons, ops — everything the Hermes agent does. Uses the Hermes model failover chain (see Hermes VPS). Reaches Newfin's /v1 API for finance answers; does not ship to customers.

docs.title: Hermes VPS
docs.text: Host: hermes@your-vps-host — runs the hermes Linux user. What it is: A full Claude Agent SDK instance — not just a cron host. Has a web dashboard (tunnel: 127.0.0.1:9119) and a Headroom LLM proxy (127.0.0.1:8787).

docs.title: Three-cron system (must not overlap)
docs.text:
Layer Owner Jobs Hermes Agent cron (dashboard → Cron tab) Hermes SDK morning-brief, journal-capture, telegram-sweep, trade-digest OS crontab (crontab -l) hermes user autodeploy, merge-poll, healthcheck, degraded-brief, intel-weekly, cbm-index, janitor-skills-audit Mac weekly-review schedule (Cowork, otherwise retired) macOS weekly-review (Sun 18:00 — the only remaining Mac-scheduled task)

Adding a job to multiple layers causes double-runs — always check all three before adding a scheduled task. (Research auto-run fully retired 2026-06-30; Persik /research is now agentic in Newfin.)

docs.title: Sync modes — vault writeback
docs.text: When Trigger What syncs Authoritative? Daily 07:30 Warsaw Scheduled daily or "morning brief" / "daily brief" Project notes ## Status (rolling 24h window), hot.md active lines, Ops board (if exists), brief ## Log Vault project notes (Status is source of truth per morning-brief.md §Source) :25 every 2h, VPS crontab Scheduled system crontab External code repos (via API), thin ## Status prepend GitHub/git repos (merge-poll.py reads via API; not a rich sync) Session-end + step 0 of morning-brief /wrap-up command OR wrap-up OR "sync projects" OR after ~/dev PR merge/push Registry: git repos, STATUS.md files, vault notes, hot.md, ops-board lanes; Linear task state (if tracker: linear) Each source type: git log, status-file hash, vault note, Linear API — code wins (project-sync.md § A.3) End of working session /wrap-up / /wrap-up all / /wrap-up merge OR wrap-up OR after code-repo merge/push Status prepend (shipped/next/blocked), brief ## Log, hot.md full overwrite, plans/catalog Latest work in session (code repo or changed vault notes); plans only if realized

docs.title: Single LLM gateway: Hermes CLI
docs.text:
All AI calls from Newfin bot, Jackie-OS skills, and Hermes agent tasks route through one gateway: the hermes CLI on the VPS. This is the Claude Agent SDK CLI. There is no direct OpenAI/Anthropic call from Newfin's backend — it goes through Hermes.

Exception: speech-to-text (Newfin voice features) calls the STT provider directly, not via Hermes CLI.

docs.title: Linear integration + autonomous agents
docs.text:
Project tracking: B-Unit is the first product tracked in Linear (workspace evegelin, project B-Unit). Task state syncs on ship per the contract in ~/dev/bunit/docs/linear-workflow.md (wrap-up hooks it), and reads back into project-sync/morning-brief via the registry tracker: linear flag (System/scripts/linear-fetch.py — see registry § Tracker switch); all other projects stay tracker: bases, markdown-only (roadmap-index.md + future-improvements.md) until Linear rolls out. New repos onboard via linear-project-rollout skill.

Autonomous agents: Two agents dispatch and auto-work on B-Unit backlog → PR → merged → Linear sync. (1) Cyrus (Claude Code) runs on Hermes VPS; (2) Codex runs in GitHub CI. Both read PRs from backlog, write and push commits, auto-sync task status to Linear on merge. Dispatch by agent is flagged in Linear issue type labels. See ~/dev/bunit/docs/linear-workflow.md for sync contract.

docs.title: How Newfin uses Hermes
docs.text: Newfin backend → SSH → hermes-ops-exec.sh (named Hermes operation) → hermes CLI → Anthropic API. @persik_hermes_bot is the direct channel to the Hermes VPS agent for all work (COO, CTO, ops). What's retired is the old relay: @Persik_finbot proxying /work commands over SSH to Hermes — that path (Persik_finbot → hermes-code-ask.py) no longer exists.

docs.title: What lives where (post-2026-06-29 restructure)
docs.text: Path Contents ~/jackie-os/ Jackie-OS repo — vault, skills, plans (git-synced every 2 min via autodeploy) ~/.hermes/ Hermes agent config: dashboard, sessions, kanban, skills packs ~/.hermes/scripts/ Symlink farm → ~/jackie-os/System/{coo,capture,ops,periodic,work,lib}/ (the repo is the source of truth; edit there, never here). Rebuilt by System/scripts/hermes-vps-link-scripts.sh ~/.hermes/skills/jackie-os Symlink → ~/jackie-os/System/skills/ (always current) ~/repos/ Read-only code clones for Hermes reference ~/jackie-os/.secrets/ Credentials (gitignored) — sourced by scripts via JACKIE_OS_ROOT

docs.title: DOCS — the master index
docs.text:
Public site: jackieos.vercel.app — landing (winner of 10 options) + docs (VPS IP + email scrubbed at build; publish: System/tools/publish-site.sh --prod). Local: bash System/tools/docs-site.sh serve → 127.0.0.1:8123. Config: docs-site/mkdocs.yml. (jackie-os-docs.vercel.app is the same deployment's legacy domain; jackie-os.vercel.app belongs to an unrelated team.)

The rule this page exists for (docs-first): before building anything new — a skill, script, worker, connector, automation — check this index for prior art. Something similar probably exists; extend it instead of adding a parallel thing. And when you ship something new, update the owning doc in the same commit (ownership map below). docs.title: Skills vs Scripts — decision
docs.text:
Skills are LLM judgment playbooks — markdown decision trees that agents follow when running a task (example: morning-brief.md = what a brief contains, how to read vault/email, when to alert, how to publish). Skills are the AI's thinking layer; they live in System/skills/ and the agent reads them whole, then improvises per context.

Scripts are the mechanics layer — bash or Python executables that handle scheduling, filesystem operations, subprocess calls, and state management (example: morning-brief-vps.py = pull vault, run the skill in the Hermes sandbox, format output, write to file, deliver). Scripts live in System/{coo,capture,ops,periodic,work,lib,scripts}/ and are the source of truth — edits go here, never the VPS copy (symlinked).

Pattern: Skills call scripts (or describe the sequence scripts follow). A typical cron job is a thin <name>.sh wrapper (cron entry) that execs a <name>.py (logic). When the LLM is involved, it's one hermes -z call returning text that the script writes.

docs.title: How it fits together (30-second orientation)
docs.text:
• Skills = markdown playbooks the AI (Claude/Hermes) follows. Some are agent-run (judgment), some are implemented mechanically by a script.
  • Scripts = the executable layer. They live in the repo under System/{coo,capture,ops,periodic,work,lib,scripts}/ and are the source of truth. On the VPS they're symlinked into ~/.hermes/scripts/ by hermes-vps-link-scripts.sh (rebuilt on every autodeploy git pull). Edit the repo copy, never the VPS copy.
  • Two schedulers: the Hermes agent-cron (~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json, edited via the dashboard — the morning stack) and the OS crontab (hermes-vps-crontab.txt — deploy/health/weekly).
  • Pattern: most cron jobs are a thin <name>.sh wrapper (cron entry) that execs a <name>.py (the logic). no_agent jobs are mechanical; the LLM, when used, is one hermes -z call returning text that the Python writes.

docs.title: Jackie OS — how to install and use it
docs.text: A shareable guide for setting up a personal knowledge OS that keeps your notes, projects, and code repos aligned — with AI as your COO, not your memory.

docs.title: For your friend (5-minute read)
docs.text:
What it is: Jackie OS is a git-backed Obsidian vault (your second brain) plus a small folder of AI "skills" (markdown playbooks) that any AI agent can run. You stay CEO — the agent is your COO and CTO: morning briefs, project status sync, research filing, and writing/shipping code. It does not rewrite your journal.

No server required. Open this folder in Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex and that tool becomes a Jackie OS agent — it auto-reads the rules and runs the skills; say wrap up and it syncs the vault. Hermes (an always-on agent on a VPS) is optional — it just runs the loop on a schedule while you sleep.

The problem it solves: You code in Cursor; Claude in a separate chat has no idea what you shipped yesterday. Notes and repos drift apart. Every session starts cold.

The minimum loop (this is the whole trick):

  1. Registry — one table maps each project to its vault note, code repo, or status file
  2. project-sync — pulls git + status files into vault ## Status (runs at session end and inside the morning brief)
  3. hot.md — a ~500-word cache agents read first so they know current focus without re-reading everything
  4. Session end — say "wrap up"; agent syncs, updates hot, commits the vault

Before / after:

Before After "What was I working on?" every morning Yesterday's brief + hot.md Code and notes disagree One sync loop, one registry Fixes lost in one repo's chat history docs/solutions/ + cross-project index

Three setup tiers — pick what fits:

Tier You get Time A — Vault PM Obsidian + vault + registry + manual sync ~30 min B — Vault + code Tier A + one code repo with bridge doc ~1 h C — Full loop Tier B + always-on automation (VPS Hermes runs the morning stack on a schedule) + merge-poll for intraday code→vault sync ~2 h + ongoing

Send your friend: this section + Quick install if they're technical, or Tier A only if they just want notes + AI briefs.

docs.title: What it is (detail)
docs.text:
Jackie OS is a git-backed Obsidian vault plus a small skill system (System/skills/). Claude (Cowork, Cursor, or Claude Code) reads the same rules every session:

  • Vault — project notes, journals, briefs, theses, clippings
  • Skills — repeatable workflows (morning brief, project sync, telegram-sweep, weekly review)
  • Project registry — maps each project to its code repo and/or STATUS.md
  • hot.md — a ~500-word cache agents read first (current focus, not history)

You stay CEO. The agent is COO: briefs, status sync, research filing — not rewriting your journal.

docs.title: What problem it solves
docs.text: Without Jackie OS With Jackie OS You code in Cursor; Claude in chat has no idea project-sync pulls git into vault ## Status Notes and repos drift apart One registry, one sync loop Every session starts cold hot.md + yesterday's brief Fixes stay in one repo docs/solutions/ + cross-project index

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Tool Role Obsidian Read/write vault (optional but ideal for daily notes) Git Version the vault and code repos Claude Code / Cursor / Codex Open the folder → it becomes a Jackie OS agent (wrap up sync at session end) GitHub Remote for vault + code repos VPS + Hermes (optional) Always-on automation — runs the morning stack on a schedule while your Mac is off Google Calendar + Gmail (optional) Morning brief connectors

No Cursor automations — all were removed 2026-06-17; Cursor is just an IDE. Code→vault sync runs via the 07:30 morning-brief (authoritative; reads merges from git log) plus a merge-poll GitHub Action in jackie-os (registry-driven, ~2h, read-only) for intraday updates. PR review on demand: /review-bugbot or /review-security in Cursor.

docs.title: 1. Clone and open
docs.text:
git clone git@github.com:YOUR_USER/jackie-os.git ~/jackie-os
cd ~/jackie-os

Open ~/jackie-os/Vault/ in Obsidian. Read order for any agent:

  1. Vault/hot.md
  2. Vault/CLAUDE.md
  3. Vault/Home.md
  4. Project note for the task

Branch note: jackie-os uses master. Code repos typically use main. Git on origin/<branch> is code truth; the vault is PM truth.

docs.title: 2. Copy the skill loop
docs.text:
Jackie OS ships skills in System/skills/. You need thin scheduled tasks in Claude Cowork that only say: "Read System/skills/X.md and follow it exactly."

Time Skill Output 07:30 morning-brief sweep → sync → brief → Persik → linking → * links.md hourly journal-capture Persik DMs → daily note Sun 18:00 weekly-review compound + Vault/Briefs/YYYY-Www brief.md

Cowork space must include vault + code folders: ~/Jackie-OS and ~/dev (see OPERATOR.md · skills/vault-rhythm/SKILL.md). Thin pointers: ~/Claude/Scheduled/*/SKILL.md → System/skills/.

Retired Cowork crons: jackie-os-telegram-sweep, jackie-os-daily-linking, jackie-os-vault-index (on demand: vault index).

docs.title: 3. Register your projects
docs.text:
New git code repo: say register project or new code project in any Jackie-OS session — agent runs System/skills/new-code-project.md (registry, vault, bridge, learnings). Then complete the Cursor UI checklist in skill § B (automations are not automatic).

Manual fallback — edit System/project-registry.md — one row per project:

Source type When to use git Code repo with GitHub remote status-file Folder project with Projects/MyThing/STATUS.md vault Dormant idea; vault note only

Add a vault note per project (Vault/My Project.md) with a ## Status section.

docs.title: 4. Bridge each code repo
docs.text:
In every code repo, add docs/JACKIE-OS.md (copy from System/templates/JACKIE-OS-bridge.md) and a line in that repo's CLAUDE.md:

After coding: push + PR merge (merge-poll Action + 07:30 brief sync the vault) or from Jackie OS say wrap up for direct pushes / vault-only work.

docs.title: 5. Code repos (siblings of Jackie-OS)
docs.text:
Code repos live outside Jackie-OS in a sibling tree (~/dev/), never nested inside it — keeps the vault git clean and avoids gitignore hacks. Pattern:

mkdir -p ~/dev
git clone git@github.com:YOUR_USER/my-app.git ~/dev/my-app

Register the path in project-registry.md as a git row (~/dev/my-app/). The vault holds knowledge about the repo in a project note; the code stays in ~/dev/. Commit code changes inside ~/dev/my-app/ separately from Jackie-OS vault commits.

docs.title: 6. Secrets (optional)
docs.text:
Telegram sweep + morning brief delivery: .secrets/telegram.env (gitignored). See System/skills/telegram-sweep.md and System/skills/morning-brief.md.

Telegram delivery: .secrets/telegram.env — see System/skills/morning-brief.md. The delivery scripts live in the repo at System/coo/ (e.g. brief-deliver-via-cron.py, brief-to-telegram.py) and are symlinked onto the VPS at ~/.hermes/scripts/ via System/scripts/hermes-vps-link-scripts.sh.

Cowork network allowlist (Settings → Capabilities): api.telegram.org, and your Newfin API host for coo-push.

docs.title: Daily workflow
docs.text:
Evening / after vault work          Morning (automatic)
        │                                │
        ▼                                ▼
  "wrap up" (vault only)          07:30 morning-brief
        │                         (sweep + sync + brief
        ├─ project-sync            + Telegram DM + coo-cache + linking)
        └─ git commit vault

  PR merge on code repo → merge-poll Action syncs vault intraday; 07:30 brief is authoritative

Rule: Git on origin/<branch> is code truth (main for apps, master for jackie-os). The vault is PM truth. Push before sync.

docs.title: Cloud / Cursor agents
docs.text: Cursor cloud agents often clone only Jackie-OS — not your external code repos or gitignored nested folders. project-sync skips missing clones and logs a warning; it does not fail the whole sync. For full sync, run wrap up or morning brief on a machine where registry paths exist locally (your Mac via Cowork is the typical source of truth).

docs.title: Roles (pick per task)
docs.text: Role Does COO (default) Briefs, sync, calendar CPO Scoping on project notes CMO Marketing projects CRO Research → Vault/Clippings/ Coach Fractal reviews — Briefs/… brief + your period notes; [[Reviews]] CTO Code in external repos

docs.title: Global agent skills (optional, Tier C)
docs.text:
One command (Jackie-OS clone on the Mac):

bash ~/Jackie-OS/System/tools/install-global-skills.sh

Installs real-file copies of global skills (previously Jackie-OS owned: jos-design-ui, jos-plan, jos-plan, jos-product-eval, agent-reach, jos-performance-check) + selective upstream (grill-for-unknowns + grill-me alias stub, teach, last30days, 3× CE) into ~/.agents/skills/. Do not bulk-install the CE plugin. Subagent map: cursor-rules.md.

Ad-hoc web reads (Exa + OpenCLI): used by research.md § Quick scout. Install mcporter + Exa:

npm install -g mcporter && mcporter config add exa https://mcp.exa.ai/mcp

For OpenCLI (Instagram/Twitter/Reddit reads), install agent-reach separately — it is no longer bundled with Jackie-OS:

pipx install https://github.com/Panniantong/Agent-Reach/archive/main.zip
agent-reach install --env=auto   # EU/US channels only; CN channels archived

Codebase memory MCP (structural code intelligence — newfin + rodyna):

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --skip-config
codebase-memory-mcp config set auto_index true

Add to ~/.cursor/mcp.json (alongside headroom):

"codebase-memory": {
  "command": "/Users/jackie/.local/bin/codebase-memory-mcp",
  "args": []
}

Restart Cursor. Routing: System/skills/codebase-memory.md.

After a non-trivial fix in a code repo:

  1. jos-compound → writes docs/solutions/ in that repo
  2. Add one index row in Jackie OS Vault/Agent-Learnings/ (never copy the full doc)
  3. jos-compound is in-session (not automated); the merge-poll Action + 07:30 morning-brief keep the vault in sync (no Cursor automation — all removed 2026-06-17)

docs.title: Customize for your life
docs.text:
Jackie OS (Sergei) Your version Vault/Theses.md Your principles or goals Projects/Newfin/ Your apps telegram-sweep Any capture inbox (email, Slack — adapt skill) Cowork 07:30 Your timezone

Keep: registry + project-sync + wrap-up + hot.md. That's the minimum loop that prevents "Claude didn't know what I shipped yesterday."

docs.text: Symptom Fix Brief missing yesterday's code work Push to GitHub, then sync projects (or wait for 07:30 brief) Brief says old state (e.g. "behind 107") but you already pulled Evening project-sync updated vault but not brief body — check brief ## Since sync or wait for tomorrow's 07:30 brief Agent overwrote my journal Hard rule: never edit inside Vault/YYYY-MM-DD.md journal bodies Two agents collided on a file git status first; multi-writer discipline in root CLAUDE.md Cowork task ran wrong logic Task must be a thin pointer to System/skills/, not inline instructions project-sync skipped my code repo Clone missing at registry path — create clone or update path in project-registry.md

Jackie OS v0 — personal AI operating system. The thinking stays yours; the system remembers the state.

docs.title: What it is
docs.text:
A second brain plus an always-on AI agent — wired together so the agent actually knows what's in the brain.

The second brain is your Obsidian vault: every journal entry, project note, decision, and idea, linked and versioned in git. It compounds over time. The agent (Hermes) lives on a server in Germany, runs 24/7, reads the vault before doing anything, and delivers results back to Telegram.

Together: you think and decide, the brain remembers, the agent acts.

docs.title: The problem this solves
docs.text:
Every time you open ChatGPT or Claude, it starts with zero context. You re-explain your projects, your priorities, what you shipped last week. The AI is helpful in a session but amnesiac across them.

Most people also have this split:

  • Notes (diary, ideas, plans) — in one app
  • Code projects — in separate folders
  • AI — in a chat window that forgot everything

Nothing shares memory. Jackie OS makes all three read from the same source.

docs.title: The second brain (vault)
docs.text:
The vault is a folder of markdown files you open in Obsidian. Notes link to each other like Wikipedia — [[Newfin]], [[Warsaw]], [[2026-06-20]]. Over time you get a web: journal connects to projects, projects connect to decisions, decisions connect to people.

What lives there:

Written by you Written by the agent Daily journal Morning brief + weekly / monthly / yearly reviews Project ideas, decisions Project ## Status (synced from code) Notes on people, places Clippings (links you sent) + person profiles Beliefs, theses Coaching notes, link suggestions, hot.md cache

hot.md is the key mechanism: after every sync, the agent writes a fresh ~500-word summary of what's currently active. Every AI session (Cursor, Claude Code, Hermes) reads this first. That's why context is never lost — there's a standing summary of where you are.

The vault is git-versioned. Nothing gets lost. The agent never edits your journal entries — only appends to the end, or writes into its own files.

Every file also carries a little structured metadata (type, title, date) in a format called OKF (Open Knowledge Format). You never see it, but it makes the vault portable — not locked to any one tool — and lets any agent orient and retrieve by metadata instead of guessing from prose.

docs.title: What it actually does
docs.text:
The system isn't one feature — it's a set of jobs the agent does for you, all reading from and writing to the same second brain.

Vaulting & linking — keeping one git-versioned source of truth and weaving it into a graph. Every note, brief, and decision lives in the vault; nothing is scattered or lost. After each brief, the agent also suggests links between notes you wrote — "this journal entry relates to [[Newfin]], to [[Warsaw]]" — so over time the vault becomes a connected web, not a pile of files.

Capturing — pulling stuff into the brain without friction. DM the Telegram bot a thought → it lands in today's journal within the hour. Send a link → it gets filed into Clippings. Type meet Sarah: with notes → it creates a meeting entry and a person note for Sarah.

Briefing — telling you where you are. Morning brief (daily), weekly review (Sunday), monthly and yearly reviews. Each reads the vault + your code and summarizes what changed, what's next, what's blocked.

Syncing — keeping code and notes in agreement. The agent reads git history from your repos and writes it into each project's ## Status note, so the vault always reflects what actually shipped.

Building — it doesn't just track your code, it writes it. Acting as your CTO (through Claude Code), the agent implements features, fixes bugs, and ships — then syncs the result back into the vault. It's COO and CTO at once.

Researching — digging on demand. Say research <topic> and it sweeps Reddit, HN, X, markets (last 30 days) and files the findings into the vault.

Coaching — the reflective layer. Recovery, identity, and "fractal" period reviews — week, month, year — where the agent takes a coach stance and walks you through patterns instead of just reporting facts.

Enriching — filling in context. New person shows up in your notes? The agent pulls a public profile and adds a ## Public profile section to their note.

Each of these is a skill — a markdown playbook the agent follows. They all share the same vault, so capturing feeds briefing, briefing feeds coaching, and nothing has to be re-explained between them.

docs.title: The agent (Hermes)
docs.text:
The jobs above are what it does. Hermes is who does them — a Claude-powered agent, not a chatbot you open. It runs 24/7 on a server, works on a schedule while you sleep, and you can reach it any time by DMing @persik_hermes_bot on Telegram. It wears two hats: COO (briefs, sync, research, journal) and CTO (writes code, builds features, ships).

Three things make it an agent rather than a script:

  • It runs itself. A schedule on the server fires the jobs — morning brief at 07:30, journal capture hourly, weekly review Sunday. Your Mac can be off and traveling; the loop still runs.
  • It follows playbooks, not hardcode. Each job is a skill — a markdown file in System/skills/ that lives in the vault. You read and edit them like any other note. Change the playbook, change the behavior.
  • It's not a black box. Everything it reads comes from the vault; everything it writes goes back to the vault. The full chain is auditable — no hidden state.

There's a second, separate bot — @Persik_finbot — that handles money and finance for the Newfin app. Hermes (@persik_hermes_bot) is the one that runs your OS.

docs.title: Hermes is optional — it lives in a folder
docs.text:
Hermes is the always-on layer: it runs the schedule on a server while you sleep. But you don't need it to use Jackie OS.

At its core, Jackie OS is just a folder of files — your notes, the skills, the rules. Open that folder in Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex and that tool becomes a Jackie OS agent. It auto-reads the same CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md rules the moment the folder is open, and the skills are right there inside it. (A few cross-project skills like wrap up are installed once on your Mac, so they work in every project.)

Nothing "migrates" — you just connect the folder. Say wrap up from any of these tools and the vault syncs, project ## Status blocks update, hot.md refreshes, and the changes commit — exactly the loop Hermes runs, just triggered by hand.

So: Hermes = the schedule (automation while you sleep). Your IDE + the folder = the same system, on demand. Same brain either way.

docs.title: How they connect
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    YOU(["You"])
    TG(["Telegram<br/>@persik_hermes_bot"])
    REPOS[("~/dev/ repos")]
    VAULT[["Vault<br/>(second brain)"]]
    HERMES{{"Hermes<br/>(agent)"}}

    YOU -->|journal| VAULT
    YOU <-->|DM| TG
    YOU -.->|read briefs| VAULT
    REPOS -->|git history| HERMES
    VAULT -->|reads everything| HERMES
    HERMES -->|## Status, briefs,<br/>clips, hot.md| VAULT
    HERMES -->|brief + replies| TG
    TG -->|your DMs| VAULT

It's a loop, not a pipeline. You feed the vault (journaling, DMs, code). Hermes reads the vault + git, does its jobs, writes back to the vault, and pings you on Telegram. Your DMs flow back into the vault. Round and round.

The glue is hot.md. When any Claude session starts — terminal, Cursor, Hermes — it reads hot.md first and walks in knowing your current focus, last merge, what's pending. That's the trick that kills the cold start.

Prefer it visual? Open JACKIE-OS-EXPLAINER.html (next to this file) in any browser — the same explainer with interactive diagrams: the loop, the eight jobs, the daily timeline, capture flow, and the cold-start/hot.md before-after. For the system diagram, see the docs site "The system map" page (bash System/tools/docs-site.sh serve) or jackie-os-docs-map.html.

docs.title: How a day actually feels
docs.text:
07:30 — Hermes wakes up (you're asleep), reads all your code repos, sees what merged, syncs project status notes, writes the brief, sends it to your Telegram. Done before you check your phone. (Research is on-demand now — say research <topic> whenever you want it; it no longer runs unattended at 06:45.)

Morning — You read the brief over coffee. Reply to Hermes via Telegram DM if you want to add something to your journal. It captures it within the hour.

Day — You work, code, journal in Obsidian. When you finish a planning session or push code, say wrap up — Hermes syncs the vault immediately.

Sunday 18:00 — Weekly review runs automatically. Patterns, what compounded, what to carry forward.

Nothing requires you. The morning stack runs on the VPS even when your Mac is off and you're traveling.

docs.title: What the agent is allowed to touch
docs.text:
Yes: - Write briefs and reviews into Vault/Briefs/ - Update ## Status blocks in project notes - Append to today's journal (Telegram capture only — end of file) - Refresh hot.md after every sync

Never: - Edit the body of your journal entries - Touch notes tagged private - Rename vault notes (that breaks Obsidian links — human-only) - Put credentials in any markdown file

docs.title: The commands (everything else is automatic)
docs.text:
The schedule covers the daily loop. These are the things you trigger by hand:

Say What it does wrap up After vault work or a code push — syncs everything now instead of waiting for 07:30 sync projects Quick mid-session "where are we?" status check research \<topic> Deep community/market dig (Reddit, HN, X, markets) filed into the vault morning brief Trigger the brief now instead of waiting coach me Reflective session — recovery, identity, patterns weekly / monthly / yearly review Run a period review on demand instead of waiting for its schedule

The morning stack, hourly journal capture, and Sunday review all run on their own — you never trigger those.

docs.title: The tools, in plain words
docs.text:
None of these need to be understood to use the system — but here's what each one is, in one line:

Tool What it is Obsidian A free notes app. Your vault is just a folder of plain text files it opens. Markdown Plain text with simple formatting (like **bold**). Future-proof — opens anywhere, forever. Git A time machine for files. Every change is saved and reversible; nothing is ever truly lost. VPS A small computer rented in a data center that never sleeps — so the agent runs even when your laptop is closed. Claude The AI model (by Anthropic) that does the actual thinking, writing, and coding. Hermes The program that turns Claude into an always-on assistant living on the VPS. Telegram The messaging app you use to talk to the agent (the bot is called Persik). Skill A markdown file of instructions telling the agent how to do one job. Editable like any note. OKF Open Knowledge Format — structured metadata (type, title, date) on every file. Makes the vault a portable, vendor-neutral bundle any agent can orient in and retrieve from — not locked to one tool.

docs.title: The core idea in one line
docs.text:
Your thinking goes into the vault. The agent reads it, acts on it, and keeps it current. You never start from zero.

Updated 2026-06-29 — morning stack on VPS Hermes cron; Mac Cowork is weekly-review only.

docs.text:
1. Journal & reviews — daily: Vault/YYYY-MM-DD.md (+ Persik). Week/month/year: read AI brief in Briefs/, then weekly review / monthly review / yearly review for your note.
  2. Build — code in ~/dev/{newfin,rodyna,draw} via Cursor (default CTO), Claude Code, or Codex — each opens the folder and becomes the same Jackie OS agent. The Hermes VPS agent also writes/ships code on its own.
  3. Close vault sessions — say wrap up when you edited Jackie-OS or Projects/ and did not just merge a PR (see below).

You do not need to remember registry paths, skill names, automation numbers, or where Status gets written.

docs.title: Scheduling deep-work blocks (agents)
docs.text:
When proposing or adding something to Sergei's calendar:

  1. Check all calendars — macOS Calendar.app (Google-synced): Life, Work, Family, Сім'я, operator@example.com, Work Unaligned, Work Flow, etc. Skip holiday/birthday/Siri-only calendars for conflict checks.
  2. Propose 2–3 free slots with duration — don't assume 10:00 is free because the user said "morning."
  3. Call out conflicts explicitly (e.g. meetings on operator@example.com or family blocks on Сім'я).
  4. Default calendar for deep work: Work. Family events stay on Family/Сім'я — don't create those without ask.
  5. After Sergei picks a slot — create the event (Calendar.app) with title, link to plan doc in description, then update hot.md + relevant plan file times.

Example (2026-06-23): Hermes Phase 0a — 10:00–12:00 blocked by Viet 11:00–12:00 → booked 12:00–15:00 on Work.

docs.title: Skill map
docs.text:
Full system map (skills + scripts, what + where-used): CATALOG.md — the newcomer entry point.

Sergei (operator): OPERATOR.md — one-page cheat sheet; what runs automatically vs what you still say.

Every skill is a markdown file in System/skills/ — vault-owned, git-versioned, tool-agnostic. Cowork scheduled tasks are thin pointers to these files; the files are the source of truth. New skills follow skills/skill-builder.md and get registered here.

Naming convention (2026-07-10): everything in System/skills/ is owned by definition — no prefix needed (and renames would break wikilinks + VPS scheduled-task pointers). The jos- prefix marks owned skills that are also symlinked into the shared global tree ~/.agents/skills/, where they sit next to upstream installs: jos-* = ours, battle-tested; unprefixed = upstream. Exception: wrap-up predates the prefix and is grandfathered unprefixed — it's referenced by dozens of docs, hooks, and habits, and still triggers on "wrap up" text; rename cost > consistency win. Hermes runs nothing outside this repo — skill playbooks live in System/skills/, executable scripts in System/{coo,capture,ops,periodic,work,lib}, symlinked onto the VPS.

docs.title: Write policy — shared / contribute-only repos (🤝)
docs.text:
A git row whose GitHub cell carries 🤝 (or whose Source shows ⚠️ shared) is a repo Sergei does not own — e.g. AleannLab/draw, co-owned with a collaborator. For these repos:

  • Sync is READ-ONLY. project-sync may diff origin/<branch> → update the vault ## Status and STATUS.md mirror. It must never push, commit, branch, or open a PR on the shared repo.
  • No Jackie-OS scaffolding. Never add docs/JACKIE-OS.md, docs/solutions/, an Agent-Learnings ## Jackie-OS sync paragraph in the repo's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, or any other Jackie-OS bookkeeping file. Bridge/learnings/compound write-ups stay on the Jackie-OS side only (vault note + Vault/Agent-Learnings/{Title} learnings.md). Skipped because: any PR there lands in the collaborator's repo. (This is the 2026-06-13 leak: backlog #2/#4 wrongly scaffolded draw — PRs #50/#51. Don't repeat it.)
  • Merge-poll: owned repos are covered by the central Action in jackie-os (registry-driven). No per-repo sync tokens or Cursor automations.
  • Only actual app changes Sergei makes himself belong in a shared repo — never agent housekeeping.

Add a row when a project gets a vault note — never hardcode paths in skills. New project (code or non-code): run skill new-code-project (registry + vault + plans scaffold + bridge + learnings + poller registration).

Plans surface (owned code repos): every new owned repo gets plans/roadmap-index.md + plans/future-improvements.md at onboarding (new-code-project § Plans scaffold). Non-code projects get Projects/{Name}/plans/. After each ship: wrap-up § Catalog cleanup.

Code-repo bridge: each owned git row should have docs/JACKIE-OS.md in the repo (template: System/templates/JACKIE-OS-bridge.md) so Cursor/Claude Code sessions know to run project-sync from Jackie-OS at session end. Shared repos (🤝) get NO bridge — see Write policy above.

docs.title: Jackie OS Planning Workflow
docs.text: This folder is the working planning surface for Jackie OS itself (skills, vault, operator, automations).

docs.title: Source of truth
docs.text:
Start with roadmap-index.md. It is audited against shipped skills, vault layout, and merged commits. If a checkbox in an older plan disagrees with what shipped, the shipped state wins and the plan should be deleted (after capturing any durable decision) or corrected.

Two ledgers, both permanent (never deleted): roadmap-index.md § Shipped (deliverables — what + when) and decisions-log.md (the durable why — locked decisions, supersessions, architecture). Plan bodies are not retained after ship; git log --full-history -- System/plans/ recovers any of them.

Runtime skills in System/skills/ are source of truth for how things run; plans are blueprints until shipped.

docs.title: Current flow
docs.text:
1. Check roadmap-index.md for the current active initiative.
  2. Read the active initiative doc in this folder (or pull from future-improvements.md for net-new work).
  3. If the initiative is still roadmap-level, create a dated implementation plan before building: YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md via jos-plan / jos-plan.
  4. When the work ships (delete-on-ship, 2026-06-29): record the deliverable in roadmap-index.md § Shipped, add any durable decision to decisions-log.md, then delete the dated plan body. No archive/ of full bodies — git history is the audit trail.
  5. Catalog cleanup (required) — in the same commit, edit future-improvements.md: remove shipped bullets, or mark 🔵 + gap only for partials; bump roadmap-index.md audit stamp. Contract: session-end § Catalog cleanup.
  6. Never delete future-improvements.md, decisions-log.md, or roadmap-index.md — prune/append, don't remove.

docs.title: File types
docs.text:
• roadmap-index.md — current status, priority order, and the Shipped deliverable ledger (permanent).
  • decisions-log.md — durable decisions/rationale ledger (permanent).
  • future-improvements.md — owner-prioritized idea catalog (stays active, no date prefix).
  • YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md — roadmap, initiative, or implementation plan (deleted on ship, after the two ledgers are updated).

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
• System/plans/ — active plans + the two permanent ledgers (roadmap-index.md, decisions-log.md).
  • History — shipped plan bodies are not kept in-tree; git log --full-history -- System/plans/ recovers them.

docs.title: Jackie-OS — Decisions Log
docs.text:
The durable why behind shipped work — locked decisions, supersession rationale, and architecture choices that outlive the plan that produced them.

Policy (2026-06-29): plan bodies are not retained after a plan ships. On ship, the deliverable goes to the roadmap-index "Shipped" table (what + when), any durable decision lands here (why), and the dated plan file is deleted — git history keeps the full body (git log --full-history -- System/plans/). This log and the roadmap Shipped table are the two ledgers; neither is ever archived.

Newest first. Keep each entry tight — link to the live skill / docs/solutions/ / CONCEPTS.md home rather than restating it.

docs.title: 2026-07-08 — OM-3: audience = template/self-host adopters; Cyrus routing on shared teams
docs.text:
Audience decision (OM-3, PM competitive review): Jackie-OS and Newfin optimize for (b) template/self-host adopters, not private-forever. Consequences executed same day: ai-os-quickstart template repo built (local, ~/dev/ai-os-quickstart, MIT — publishing still an owner action), Newfin onboarded to Linear with adopter-facing backlog (EVE-52..57), deployment/docs work queued. Published 2026-07-09: sc-jackie/ai-os-quickstart — public, is_template=true; Jackie-OS stays private.

Cyrus routing labels are repo-unique on a shared team. With multiple repos on team EVE, Pipeline labels (dev…) cannot route — B-Unit claims them. Each repo routes on its project-name label (Newfin, created as workspace label). linear-project-rollout § 3 corrected.

Newfin prod migrations: VPS autodeploy is the only auto path. db-migrate.yml's push trigger died 2026-06-26; hermes-vps-autodeploy.sh (*/2 cron) runs supabase db push on migration change (verified live with N7's monotonic-guard). Manual path = deploy-migrations.yml one-click button (pooler URL). db-migrate.yml deleted.

docs.title: 2026-07-04 — Knowledge approval on morning brief; journal-linking v2 semantic
docs.text:
Knowledge write-back approval lives on the Persik brief attachment, not Hermes. After VPS brief-deliver-via-cron.py renders the HTML brief, it scans rated 4–5 read clips and attaches inline buttons via Newfin coo-brief-deliver → sendDocument + reply_markup. Taps call VPS knowledge append|ignore {kn_slug} (knowledge-integrate-approved.py applies pre-drafted proposals from Vault/Briefs/* knowledge-candidates.md). Agents still draft proposals; Sergei approves via button or explicit "integrate knowledge".

Journal-linking v2 = semantic pass only. v1 mechanical inbound linker (References mentions) stays no-LLM. v2 adds one optional hermes -z JSON pass for illuminate-together edges on notes touched in the last 48h (DAILY_LINK_SEMANTIC=0 disables). Person-enrich is not a cron job — it stays on-demand via meeting-capture / enrich {Name} (web research, agent session).

Consolidation Tier 0 closed: orphaned Archive/System-plans/, Archive/_Command Center/, and System/Archive/ removed; operator changelog at Archive/operator-changelog.md. Telegraph extract (Tier 3) cancelled — Telegraph retired 2026-06-20.

Plans catalog policy (2026-07-04): when operational work from a dated plan is done, delete the plan body and move any product/strategic remainder to future-improvements. Jackie-OS System/plans/ now holds only this index, decisions-log, future-improvements, and README — no active dated plans. Newfin/Hermes split operational phase (Tracks A+B, two-bot) is complete; OSS, unified front door (C8), and dashboards deferred to the catalog.

docs.title: 2026-07-01 — Self-improving skills: feedback ledger + approve-gated skill-improve loop
docs.text:
Skills are procedural memory; without a feedback loop they're tech debt (Warp/Anthropic; Nous Hermes-agent curator pattern). Added a native loop rather than installing a plugin (UniM0cha/claude-self-improving-skills and friends are Claude-Code-hook-only, write to ~/.claude/skills/, and mostly auto-patch — none fit the vault-as-source-of-truth model or the vault's no-auto-rewrite contract).

Shape: skill-feedback is an append-only ledger (capture only — no edits). skill-improve reads open rows, drafts one concrete diff per skill, and stops for Sergei's approval before applying — matching skill-builder's conscious-agent contract. Wiring reuses existing loops (no new cron): session-end captures ambient feedback (step 4b); weekly-review step 0 runs the curator pass (propose diffs + prune ledger).

Borrowed from the proven tools, minus auto-patch: provenance footer + improve_count: telemetry in skill frontmatter (skill-builder), weekly curator/consolidation, and rollback-by-git (one skill per commit → clean git revert; no backup files). Boundary: jos-compound = code fixes (docs/solutions/); skill-improve = skill-behavior (the .md itself).

docs.title: 2026-07-01 — VPS agent-skills → mechanical harness; ops alerts → one gateway
docs.text:
Two locked calls from closing the journal-linking gap and the ops-routing loose ends:

Agent-skills don't run on VPS cron — re-architect as a mechanical harness. Every VPS cron job is no_agent: it shells hermes -z <prompt> for one-shot text, and the Python script writes the files. There is no file-editing agent loop. So skills that edit multiple vault files (daily-linking, person-enrich) can't run "folded into morning-brief" as documented. The pattern that works is the one every cron already uses: Python harness does the deterministic file ops; the LLM (if needed) is one hermes -z call returning a judgment. daily-linking v1 needs no LLM at all — Vault/References/ is a bounded, known entity set, so an inbound linker (journal mention of a known person/place → ## See also) is pure whole-word matching. Semantic edges are the only part that needs hermes -z; deferred to v2. (daily-linking-vps.py.)

Agent-cron entries MUST be shims, not symlinks (AGENT_CRON_ENTRIES in hermes-vps-link-scripts.sh): the Hermes cron rejects any entry that resolves outside ~/.hermes/scripts/. A symlinked .sh fails the path-check; a shim (exec bash <repo-path>) passes. New agent-cron .sh wrappers must be added to that list.

Ops alerts route through one place — hermes-ops-notify.sh (gateway → @persik_hermes_bot, finbot fallback). Scripts that hand-roll their own POST to Newfin /api/cron/ops-notify land on @Persik_finbot (the finance bot), which owns the only bot token in that repo. Ops/CI/deploy/janitor alerts belong on the Hermes bot. Every notifier shells the one .sh; hermes-intel-weekly is the sole intended direct-to-finbot sender (it's a finance digest). Journal-capture (mechanical) + this linker are complementary, not duplicates.

docs.text:
1. Vault/hot.md — then CLAUDE.md, Vault/CLAUDE.md
  2. [[About me]] — hold goal order: recover → habits → meaning → direction (#4 premature = identity re-attachment)
  3. [[Theses]] — flag contradictions/complications; don't flatter
  4. Latest [[Self-portraits]] + [[Coaching]] index
  5. For depth: [[Psychological synthesis 2026-06]] or [[Observations by Claude]] ([[Syntheses]]) — outside reading only
  6. Never load notes tagged private or #private

docs.title: Coaching stance (best practices)
docs.text:
Relationship - Sergei is the thinker; Claude illuminates, challenges, structures — does not delegate understanding ([[Style guide]]). - Engage hard material fully ([[Self-portrait 2026-03]]); no "talk to a professional" deflection — he has psychiatrist + therapist; encourage bringing session insights to them when safety-relevant. - Recovery frame: not "are you over it?" but what gets built next, with more wisdom.

Listening & inquiry (ICF-aligned, adapted) - Reflect back mechanism, not mood only ("sounds like shame → escape → more shame"). - One powerful question at a time when stuck; don't stack five. - Distinguish resistance (fear, misalignment) from misalignment (wrong path) — ask which. - Name rationalization directly when seen; cite journal or behavior evidence. - Separate emotional weather from objective facts (portfolio, shipped PRs).

Accountability without shame - Track commitments as experiments, not moral scores. - Celebrate process (showed up, journaled, closed position) separate from outcomes. - Gaming/trading hours climbing = overload signal, not character failure ([[Self-portrait 2026-03]]).

Recurrence risks (flag early) - Identity attaching to a new metric (subscribers, revenue, ship count, fitness). - "Productive" avoidance: tooling, research, vault notes without ships. - Skipping goal order in [[About me]] because direction feels urgent. - Comparison spirals (peers, age, Google-at-tennis moments).

What not to do - Toxic positivity; "others have it worse"; "everything happens for a reason". - Clinical diagnosis or medication advice. - Rewrite [[About me]] or self-portraits without Sergei asking. - Edit journal content; evergreens unless asked (Sergei writes those).

docs.title: On-demand session shape (light)
docs.text:
1. Where are you? — mood, energy, sleep, one line (ask if missing).
  2. What's live? — one tension or decision; don't boil the ocean.
  3. Evidence — pull 1–3 journal lines or Status facts if relevant.
  4. Mechanism — name the pattern if visible (conditional worth, avoidance, merger/escape).
  5. One question — for Sergei's reflection.
  6. Optional next step — one experiment for 7 days, not a life plan.

docs.text: Inherited vault hard rules apply. Period reviews are a lens, not a replacement for Sergei's own review or therapy.

docs.title: codebase-memory
docs.text: Purpose: structural code intelligence via codebase-memory-mcp — call graphs, routes, impact analysis, architecture overview. Machine-local MCP in Cursor (and Claude Code if configured). Trigger: "what calls X?", blast radius, find routes/entry points, dead code, cross-file trace, unfamiliar codebase orientation. Role: CTO tooling (read-only graph queries — not edits, not web). Scope: ~/dev/newfin, ~/dev/rodyna only — not Jackie-OS vault.

docs.title: When to use
docs.text:
Question Use first Not Known bug / documented fix docs/solutions/ grep codebase-memory What calls / is called by X? trace_path many grep/read cycles Routes, packages, entry points get_architecture reading whole app.ts / registry.ts Symbol by name pattern search_graph SemanticSearch alone "Where is auth handled?" (fuzzy) semantic_query WebSearch Uncommitted change blast radius detect_changes manual diff + grep Read one function body get_code_snippet after graph lookup Read whole file Broad unfamiliar area get_architecture → targeted trace_path explore for everything Exact text in files Grep / search_code graph tools

Hard rule: graph for structure; Grep/Read for exact text and edits; docs/solutions/ for documented fixes. Never skip jos-compound learnings.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. get_architecture — languages, packages, routes, hotspots (first move in unfamiliar work).
  2. search_graph — find exact symbol (name_pattern, label: Function, Method, Route, Class).
  3. trace_path — inbound/outbound call chain (direction: both | inbound | outbound; depth 1–5).
  4. get_code_snippet — qualified name from step 2; then Read only lines you will edit.
  5. detect_changes — before risky edits on dirty tree.

Other tools: query_graph (Cypher subset), search_code, manage_adr, index_status, list_projects.

docs.text:
Step Command / path Binary curl -fsSL …/install.sh \| bash -s -- --skip-config → ~/.local/bin/codebase-memory-mcp Cursor MCP ~/.cursor/mcp.json → server codebase-memory Auto-index codebase-memory-mcp config set auto_index true Cache ~/.cache/codebase-memory-mcp/ Update codebase-memory-mcp update Uninstall codebase-memory-mcp uninstall (agent configs only)

Restart Cursor after MCP changes. Verify: Settings → MCP → codebase-memory with 14 tools.

One repo per Cursor window (cursor-rules.md) — index matches the open project. Say "Index this project" on first use if auto-index did not run.

Auto-link only high-confidence connections; report the rest for Sergei to confirm. Trigger: last step of morning-brief after brief delivery + coo-cache (preferred), or on demand "daily linking". Standalone Cowork jackie-os-daily-linking is retired — disable that scheduled task. When folded into morning-brief: write only — the brief run's single end-of-run commit includes links.md. Role: COO. Output: Vault/Briefs/YYYY-MM-DD links.md (its own file — never the brief note). Model: Haiku 4.5 — the "illuminate-together" test is structural (do two notes co-explain a third concept?), not deep reasoning. Inputs are capped at ~30 notes, most outputs are 5 auto-links + a Review list. Sonnet/Opus is over-spec; promote individual hard calls to Sonnet manually if a run flags an ambiguous edge.

docs.title: What this skill is for (and what it isn't)
docs.text: There are two link systems in the vault. Backlinks (Obsidian's panel) are automatic and complete — every [[wikilink]] that already exists shows up for free, no maintenance. This skill does not chase volume; backlinks already cover that. Its job is the few strong edges Obsidian can't surface on its own — pairs of notes that illuminate each other but were never explicitly linked. "Smart" means selective, not prolific. Never auto-link on shared topic alone — reading the two together must reveal something neither does alone ([[Style guide]] standard). Respect first-mention-only; don't link-spam.

docs.title: How journals participate
docs.text:
Journals (dated YYYY-MM-DD.md at vault root + yearly Journals/Archive/Journal 20XX.md) are archive material — hard rule: never edit their inner content (Vault/CLAUDE.md). They join the graph in two ways, weighted toward the first:

  1. INBOUND (primary, always safe). When a journal connects to a stable note (evergreen, reference/person, place, thesis), add the link on the stable note, pointing into the journal — never touch the journal. This is the highest-value direction (it answers "where did this come from?") and the pattern the vault already uses (e.g. Mari.md → "runs through [[Journal 2017]], [[Journal 2018]]"). Put it in the stable note's ## See also (create one if absent).
  2. Old content → anchor to the yearly Journal 20XX note (the stable linkable unit). Current content → the specific daily YYYY-MM-DD.md.
  3. FOOTER (secondary, sparing). Only when a journal entry clearly seeded a specific evergreen, append a ## See also block at the very end of that journal — below Sergei's writing, never woven into it (same append-only precedent as journal-capture). One or two links max; if unsure, prefer inbound instead and leave it for Review.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
Read first: CLAUDE.md (root), Vault/CLAUDE.md, Vault/Style guide.md. Inputs: all vault notes created/modified in the last 24h (skip .obsidian/ and Claude's own Briefs/). Journals are now in scope — but only via the two mechanisms above; their inner content is still read-for-context-only.

Bound the load (token economy): cap inputs at ~30 notes, most-recently-modified first (list any overflow under Review). Load stable / non-journal notes in full, but read journals by title + first-mention scan only, not full body — that's enough to spot the 0–5 strong edges without pulling every appended line into context.

  1. Auto-link (strong only) — connections that clearly meet the standard and are unambiguous (one obvious target, no competing candidates). Add the wikilink per the rules above (inbound on the stable note; footer on the journal only for clear evergreen seeds). Cap: 5 auto-links per run — if more qualify, link the 5 strongest and list the rest under Review.
  2. Review (everything else) — plausible-but-not-certain connections, or any with competing targets: list the wikilinks + one line on what reading them together reveals. Sergei confirms; do not link these.
  3. Write the log — Vault/Briefs/YYYY-MM-DD links.md: what was auto-linked (with the one-line rationale each, marked INBOUND or FOOTER) and the Review candidates. Empty day → one line saying so; create no links.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: Never auto-link on shared topic alone — illuminate, don't just relate. Wikilinks only. Never edit journal inner content; the only journal write allowed is an append-only ## See also footer at the end, and only for a clear evergreen seed. Never rename notes. For inbound links, keep the added line structural and sourced (where the connection lives + a short anchor), not a new interpretation — distilling the meaning is Sergei's job, not the linker's (don't delegate understanding). Don't touch a note dirty in git status from another writer (multi-writer discipline) — list it under Review instead. Standalone run: git commit — Daily linking YYYY-MM-DD. Folded into morning-brief: no commit here.
