docs.title: janitor
docs.text: Purpose: maintain the vault and the AI system itself — six modes: cascade, harmonize, vault-audit, skills-audit, link-gardening, status-archive. Trigger: "janitor", or any mode name (status-archive, vault-audit, …). Also: weekly review may queue janitor work it discovered.

docs.title: Modes
docs.text:
cascade — propagate a name change everywhere: body-text wikilinks, frontmatter categories, aliases, file paths in CLAUDE.md/System/, scheduled-task pointers. NOTE: the rename itself happens in Obsidian UI only (hard rule — it updates wikilinks natively); cascade covers what Obsidian misses (plain-text paths, system files, prompts). Journal files: update links, never the surrounding content.

harmonize — propagate a convention change (new frontmatter field, heading structure, label) across all notes sharing the convention. Show the diff plan first: which notes, what changes. Execute on confirmation.

vault-audit — check Home.md, Style guide.md, Vault/CLAUDE.md, Evergreens.md, Idea Factory 🏭.md against reality (Milo's navigation/creation-janitor): dead wikilinks, listed notes that don't exist, existing project notes missing from Home, Idea Factory index vs idea notes, templates that drifted from actual note structure, stale MOCs. Report; fix on request.

skills-audit — check every file in System/skills/ against the skill-builder schema and SKILLS.md against the folder contents. Fix drift: unregistered skills, registered skills that don't exist, schema violations, scheduled tasks whose pointers are broken.

link-gardening — periodic full lint. Mechanics: walk every vault .md (skip .obsidian/), build two sets — all wikilink targets used, all note titles that exist — and diff them. Report in four buckets: dead links (link → no note), orphans (note with no inbound links, 30+ days old) with one suggested connection each, frontmatter gaps (notes missing the [[Style guide]] standard), link density (notes overdue for first-mention links vs link-spammed). Report → confirm → fix; never auto-delete an orphan.

status-archive (alias: status-trim) — trim long ## Status logs on active project notes. For each registry row with Active = yes, read Vault/{note}.md ## Status: keep the 5 newest dated blocks (*YYYY-MM-DD… lines); delete older blocks. Full history lives in git (git log -p -- Vault/{note}.md) — no vault archive folder. Preserve any content after the Status blocks (e.g. ## Backlog, ## Projects) unchanged. Never touch journal files. Report blocks removed per project. Run quarterly or when a Status section exceeds ~80 lines.

okf-lint — verify all files in the OKF bundle have required frontmatter. Check all System/skills/**/*.md for type, title, timestamp fields; report missing ones.

python3 - <<'PY'
import re
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path.home() / "Jackie-OS"
REQUIRED = {"type", "title", "timestamp"}

errors = []
for md in sorted((ROOT / "System" / "skills").rglob("*.md")):
    if "archive" in md.parts:
        continue
    content = md.read_text()
    if not content.startswith("---"):
        errors.append(f"MISSING frontmatter: {md.relative_to(ROOT)}")
        continue
    end = content.find("\n---", 3)
    fm = content[3:end]
    present = set(re.findall(r"^(\w+):", fm, re.MULTILINE))
    missing = REQUIRED - present
    if missing:
        errors.append(f"MISSING {missing}: {md.relative_to(ROOT)}")

for e in errors:
    print(e)
print(f"\n{len(errors)} issues found.")
PY

Report: list of files with missing fields + count.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: Janitor changes structure, never meaning — if a fix would alter what a note says, stop and ask. Batch report → confirm → execute; no silent mass edits. Commit per mode run.

docs.title: journal-capture
docs.text: Purpose: drain Persik owner journal queue → append-only to today's Obsidian daily note (Vault/YYYY-MM-DD.md). Hourly capture while Mac is on. (Hermes deferred — revisit on travel.) Trigger: Cowork 0 * * * * (jackie-os-journal-capture) while Mac is on · on demand "flush journal" · "journal capture". Role: COO. Output: appended journal blocks in Vault/YYYY-MM-DD.md; journal_inbox rows marked applied. Model: Haiku 4.5 — this task is mechanical (fetch queue → group by date → verbatim append with HH:MM stamp → PATCH applied). No reasoning, no interpretation, no condensation. Sonnet/Opus is wasted spend on the hourly cadence.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
1. Load .secrets/newfin-cron.env: CRON_SECRET, NEWFIN_API_BASE.
  2. GET $NEWFIN_API_BASE/api/cron/journal-inbox?status=pending&limit=20 with Bearer CRON_SECRET. Each entry carries: text (extracted body for media rows; otherwise verbatim journal line), media_caption (owner Telegram caption when set), media_storage_path / media_filename / media_kind when a PDF or photo is attached, forward_from when forwarded, journal_date, captured_at.
  3. If empty → stop (report 0). Do this before any git pull — the common case (≈23h/day) exits here with zero git work. 3b. Lock-contention defer (before any append). Queue is non-empty, so a commit is coming. First check whether another writer holds the repo: 
    cd ~/Jackie-OS && ls .git/index.lock .git/HEAD.lock 2>/dev/null
    If a lock prints, wait ~10s and re-check once. If it still prints → abort this run cleanly: do not git pull, do not append, do not PATCH. The entries stay pending and the next hourly tick drains them. Report deferred: lock contention. This is the safety valve that keeps the hourly task from competing with the 07:30 morning-brief on a laptop-wake catch-up — journal-capture is append-only and idempotent only if it never half-writes, so it yields rather than races. (journal-capture never clears a lock or calls the file-delete grant — that's morning-brief/wrap-up's job as the privileged writer.)
  4. git pull Jackie-OS (Hermes host) — only now that there's something to append.
  5. Group entries by journal_date. For each date, target Vault/{journal_date}.md:
  6. File missing — create from Vault/Templates/Journal entry.md (frontmatter: categories: [[Journals]]/[[Daily]], created: {date}).

  7. Append only — never edit or delete existing lines. After existing body, append:

    ---

**HH:MM** (Telegram)

{verbatim text — for media rows this is media_caption when set, else text}

![[Attachments/persik/YYYY-MM-DD/{id}-{filename}]]

> {optional: first ~400 chars of text when media_caption is set and text is the PDF/vision extract}

    Use Europe/Warsaw wall time from captured_at for HH:MM. Media rows (media_storage_path set): before append, run bash ~/.hermes/scripts/persik-media-fetch.sh {id} Vault/Attachments/persik/{captured_at date}/{id}-{media_filename} (create Vault/Attachments/persik/ if missing). Omit the ![[…]] line if fetch fails (flag in report; still append caption). Omit the > extract block when there is no caption or extract. 6. One git commit per run if any files changed: Journal capture YYYY-MM-DD (+N entries). 7. For each applied entry: PATCH $NEWFIN_API_BASE/api/cron/journal-inbox/{id} body {"status":"applied"}. 8. Report: N entries, which dates touched.

docs.title: B-Unit day log (folded)
docs.text: After step 5 (journal append, before commit), run System/capture/b_unit_day_log_sync.py for each journal_date touched — copies Telegram blocks that start with B-Unit: / bunit: / Bim day: into the matching visit curriculum/week-*/day-NN.md → ## Done → ### YYYY-MM-DD. Spec: b-unit-day-log. Same commit as journal capture when files change.

docs.title: Meeting capture (folded)
docs.text: After step 8, follow meeting-capture for kind=meeting rows (same run, same lock-yield rules). Meeting rows append to the daily and index Vault/References/{Person}.md — they do not use a separate Meetings/ folder.

docs.title: Finance intent edge cases (Persik side)
docs.text: Owner plain text routes to journal unless finance heuristics match (portfolio terms, NW/crypto/runway questions, money + context). Ambiguous → journal; user can /ask for CFO. Documented in Newfin server/src/lib/journal-intent.ts.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Append-only — the only allowed mutation inside Vault/YYYY-MM-DD.md for agents. Never rewrite Sergei's prior journal prose.
  • Credentials in queued text → do not write; PATCH applied anyway and flag in report.
  • Wife/spouse/group never enqueue — Persik routes them to finance advisor only (no journal API exposure needed).
  • One runner at a time — Mac Cowork is the runner (duplicate append risk if a second one is ever added). (Hermes deferred — revisit on travel.)
  • Yield on lock, never clear it — if Jackie-OS git is locked, defer per step 3b (carry entries to next hour). Do not delete locks; morning-brief clears via jackie-os-git-native.sh on the Mac.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Mac today (Cowork): enable jackie-os-journal-capture in Cowork scheduled tasks — cron 0 * * * * (hourly), folder Jackie-OS. Keep the Mac awake or plugged in; entries queue until the next run if Cowork misses a tick. Say flush journal for immediate drain.

Full journal-capture rollout: live VPS: hermes-ops.md · decisions: decisions-log § Hermes off-Mac.

Requires Newfin migration journal_inbox applied and Persik journal router deployed.

docs.title: knowledge-integration
docs.text: Purpose: turn filed sources, research, and approved insights into sparse Knowledge maps without creating a second read-later queue or rewriting journals. Trigger: "integrate knowledge", "append to Knowledge", "process this clipping", "knowledge candidates", high-rated clips during morning brief, or explicit user approval after an agent proposes write-back. Role: COO / research assistant. AI classifies and drafts; Sergei approves semantic write-back. Output: updates to Vault/Knowledge.md, Vault/Knowledge/*.md, optional concept notes, and clipping frontmatter knowledge_state.

docs.title: Read first
docs.text:
1. CLAUDE.md
  2. Vault/CLAUDE.md
  3. Vault/Style guide.md
  4. Vault/Knowledge.md
  5. Relevant Vault/Knowledge/*.md
  6. Source clipping(s) in Vault/Clippings/

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
The vault has four layers:

  • Journal - what happened and what Sergei thought. Append-only; never rewrite.
  • Clipping - external source filed once in Vault/Clippings/.
  • Knowledge - reusable models, maps, best sources, and source-backed concepts.
  • Evergreen/Thesis - personal worldview or load-bearing belief, only promoted with Sergei's reflection.

docs.title: Classification
docs.text:
AI does first-pass classification.

  • Assign 1-3 Knowledge domains.
  • Assign 1-5 subtopics from the domain maps.
  • Use existing subtopic names where possible.
  • If no domain fits, add needs-taxonomy and ask before changing the taxonomy.
  • If confidence is low, leave a review note instead of mutating Knowledge.

Clip frontmatter may include:

topics: [ai, design, ai-tooling]
knowledge_domains:
  - "[[AI]]"
  - "[[Design and product taste]]"
knowledge_subtopics:
  - AI tooling
  - Agents and workflows
knowledge_state: inbox # inbox | candidate | integrated | ignored

State rules:

  • inbox - filed but not yet worth integration.
  • candidate - read/rated/high-signal and ready for proposed extraction.
  • integrated - approved write-back completed.
  • ignored - reviewed and deliberately not integrated.

docs.title: Extraction
docs.text:
AI drafts extraction; Sergei approves.

Trigger extraction when:

  • source is read and rated 4-5,
  • Sergei says "extract this" or "append to Knowledge",
  • a research note was explicitly requested for filing and integration,
  • several clips point to the same reusable concept.

Draft format before approval:

## Proposed Knowledge write-back

Source: [[Clipping title]]
Domains: [[AI]], [[Design and product taste]]
Subtopics: AI tooling; Frontend implementation quality

Proposed additions:
- Best sources: why this source is worth returning to.
- Working models: one source-backed claim in Sergei-safe wording.
- Map: any subtopic update needed.
- Concept note: yes/no, with proposed title.

Needs Sergei reflection:
- Personal take, belief update, project decision, or thesis/evergreen promotion if applicable.

docs.title: Write-back rules
docs.text:
After explicit approval, AI may:

  • add a source to ## Best sources,
  • add a concise source-backed bullet to ## Working models,
  • update ## Map subtopic descriptions,
  • create a concept note from Vault/Templates/Concept note.md,
  • mark the clipping knowledge_state: integrated.

AI must not:

  • invent Sergei's personal take,
  • promote anything to [[Theses]] or [[Evergreens]] without explicit reflection,
  • rewrite journals or journal archive content,
  • copy large external text into the vault,
  • turn domain maps into queues,
  • duplicate a source note across domains.

docs.title: Domain map rules
docs.text:
Each domain map is a thinking surface with:

## Why this matters
## Questions
## Map
## Best sources
## Working models

## Uses is optional when projects or life areas are helpful.

Split a subtopic into a new note only when it has 7+ meaningful links or concepts, appears across multiple projects, or becomes something Sergei asks agents about directly.

docs.title: Morning brief behavior
docs.text:
Morning brief may surface:

  • oldest unread clips from [[Read Later]],
  • rated 4-5 clips with knowledge_state missing or candidate,
  • open questions from Knowledge maps that are relevant to current projects.

Morning brief must not integrate candidates automatically. It should ask for a one-click approval path such as "append to Knowledge", "ignore", or "ask me later".

docs.title: Telegram approval buttons
docs.text:
When brief-deliver-via-cron.py runs after the morning brief, it attaches inline buttons to the HTML brief document on @Persik_finbot (via Newfin POST /api/cron/coo-brief-deliver → sendDocument + reply_markup):

  • Append to Knowledge → kn:a:{kn_slug} → VPS knowledge append {slug} → knowledge-integrate-approved.py
  • Ignore → kn:i:{kn_slug} → sets clip knowledge_state: ignored
  • Ask later → kn:l:{kn_slug} → ack only; clip stays candidate

Candidates need kn_slug in clip frontmatter (or a hash fallback). Proposed write-backs live in Vault/Briefs/YYYY-MM-DD knowledge-candidates.md until approved.

docs.title: Research behavior
docs.text: Before external research, read Vault/Knowledge.md and relevant domain maps. State what the vault already knows and what is still open. After research, propose write-back; do not silently mutate Knowledge unless Sergei explicitly requested integration.

docs.title: learning
docs.text:
Purpose: bridge personal multi-session learning (teach global skill) into Jackie-OS — fixed workspace paths, vault hub notes, promotion on wrap-up. Trigger: teach me <topic>, learning session <topic>, /teach (read this file first), learning wrap-up. Role: COO / Coach-adjacent (skills acquisition, not identity work — see coaching). Output: Learning/<slug>/ workspace artifacts; Vault/Learn {Topic}.md hub; optional brief ## Log + hot.md on wrap-up.

Folders: Jackie-OS only for writes. Safe from jackie-dev multi-root — never use ambient CWD.

docs.title: When to use
docs.text: Sergei wants… Skill Stress-test a plan before building grill-me (global) Multi-session curriculum on a personal/general topic learning (this) + global teach Technical fix documentation jos-compound → repo docs/solutions/ + [[agent-learnings-index]] Saved links / research research → [[Clippings]] Identity, recovery, direction coaching

docs.title: Process — start (teach me … / learning session)
docs.text:
1. Read Vault/hot.md. If topic missing, ask once.
  2. Slug — lowercase kebab from topic (Polish → polish).
  3. Workspace root — ~/Jackie-OS/Learning/<slug>/ (create if missing):
  4. lessons/, learning-records/, reference/, assets/
  5. Hub — create or open Vault/Learn {Topic}.md (title-case topic). Template below.
  6. Mission — if MISSION.md empty/missing, interview per upstream teach (concrete outcome, not "understand X"). Write MISSION.md; mirror summary in hub ## Mission.
  7. Teach — load global teach skill (~/.agents/skills/teach/SKILL.md). All artifact writes go under the workspace root above. Shell working_directory = that path. Never write teach artifacts to Jackie-OS root, Vault/, or ~/dev/*.
  8. After each lesson: increment lessons/000N-….html; link from hub ## Progress.

docs.title: Process — wrap-up (learning wrap-up)
docs.text:
1. Scan learning-records/ for records that qualify (demonstrated understanding, prior knowledge stated, misconception fixed, mission shift — not mere coverage).
  2. Promote qualifying records → hub ## Progress (title + 1–2 sentences). Full files stay in workspace.
  3. Best resources from RESOURCES.md → file as [[Clippings]] when stable; wikilink from hub ## Resources.
  4. Update hub ## Status (date, next ZPD focus). Sync mission summary if MISSION.md changed.
  5. If focus shifted materially → Vault/hot.md one line; today's Vault/Briefs/YYYY-MM-DD brief.md ## Log if brief exists.
  6. Durable insights in Sergei's voice → root evergreen + [[Evergreens]]; end with an open question when the insight is still a door (see [[Evergreens]]).

docs.title: Hub note template (Vault/Learn {Topic}.md)
docs.text:
---
categories:
  - "[[Learning]]"
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---

# Learn {Topic}

## Mission

(3–5 lines from workspace MISSION.md)

## Workspace

`Learning/<slug>/`

## Progress

- (promoted learning records + lesson links)

## Resources

- (wikilinks to Clippings / References)

## Status

Last session: — · Next: —

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• No Vault/Learning/ folder — hub notes at vault root only ([[Style guide]]).
  • No teach HTML or learning-records/ inside Vault/.
  • No Agent-Learnings rows for personal topics (technical index only).
  • No Cowork schedule — on-demand only ([[Theses]] #1: mission required, not open-ended tooling).
  • Tie every session to a concrete mission; push back on vagueness (upstream teach rule).

docs.title: linear-project-rollout
docs.text:
Replicate the workflow proven on B-Unit (2026-07-07) onto another repo. Delegate a Linear issue → an agent builds it → PR → you review + merge → (migration? one-click deploy).

Realistic scope: one prompt does everything scriptable; two browser steps per repo are irreducible (Codex env + Linear↔GitHub connect). Not truly one-click, but close.

Run after new-code-project has done the base wiring (registry, vault note, bridge). This adds the Linear/agents layer on top.

docs.title: Already set up once — REUSED for every repo (don't redo)
docs.text: Thing Where Notes Linear workspace evegelin, team Evegelin (key EVE, 48daea3d-b403-4c71-b6c3-984db6b83fc4) Linear one team for all repos Cyrus (Claude Code agent) Hermes — cyrus.service + cyrus-ngrok.service add repos with cyrus self-add-repo; see [[cyrus-claude-code-linear-agent-hermes]] Linear "Claude Code" OAuth app (the Cyrus agent) Linear workspace direct webhooks; LINEAR_DIRECT_WEBHOOKS=true Codex GitHub connector ChatGPT / GitHub (sc-jackie) per-repo env still needed (browser) Workspace label groups — Pipeline (dev/content/research) · Stage (needs-refinement/needs-approval) · Type (Bug/Feature/Improvement) Linear workspace-scoped, shared across every project — nothing to recreate per repo

docs.title: The one prompt (paste into a Claude Code session opened in the target repo)
docs.text:
Requires: the session has the Linear MCP connected, and ssh hermes works from the machine.

Onboard this repo into our Linear + agents workflow per
~/Jackie-OS/System/skills/linear-project-rollout.md. Do the scriptable parts, then hand me
the two browser steps. Steps:

1. LINEAR PROJECT (MCP): create a project named "<Repo>" under team EVE
   (48daea3d-b403-4c71-b6c3-984db6b83fc4). Labels need NOTHING created — the 3 workspace groups
   (Pipeline: dev/content/research · Stage: needs-refinement/needs-approval · Type:
   Bug/Feature/Improvement) already apply to every project. Get the new project id.

2. OPERATING MANUAL (files): copy ~/dev/bunit/docs/linear-workflow.md into this repo's docs/,
   swap the IDs block (workspace/team/project/board). Labels are workspace-shared — no per-repo
   label edits. (Optional: a content/marketing arm → its own project, per that doc's
   "Content vs. product" section.)
   IF this repo has supabase/migrations/, ALSO copy from ~/dev/bunit:
   .github/workflows/deploy-migrations.yml, .github/workflows/migration-notice.yml,
   scripts/ci/linear-migration-notice.sh, scripts/codex-setup.sh — and drop the one-time
   `repair` step from deploy-migrations.yml (bunit-specific; a fresh project won't need it).

3. CYRUS (ssh hermes): `cyrus self-add-repo <https-git-url> evegelin`. Keep the DEFAULT
   routingLabels it sets (the repo/project name, e.g. `["Newfin"]`) — on a shared team,
   Pipeline labels (`dev`/…) can't route because another repo already claims them (B-Unit
   routes on `dev`/`curriculum`/`bim`; discovered 2026-07-08). Create the matching
   workspace label in Linear if missing, and put that label on every issue meant for this
   repo's agent. Then `systemctl --user restart cyrus.service`.

4. SEED BACKLOG (MCP): read plans/roadmap-index.md (or scan the code) and create 5-10 Backlog
   issues, each intent-level (title + one-line why), labeled needs-refinement + a Pipeline label.

5. VAULT: add the Linear board URL to this repo's row in ~/Jackie-OS/System/project-registry.md.

6. Commit the repo changes on a branch → PR → merge. Then run /wrap-up.

Finally, print the TWO BROWSER STEPS I must do myself (Codex env + Linear↔GitHub connect,
per the skill), and stop.

docs.title: The two browser steps (per repo, ~3 min — the prompt can't do these)
docs.text:
1. Codex Cloud env — chatgpt.com/codex → Environments → Create → select the repo → Setup script: bash /workspace/<repo>/scripts/codex-setup.sh (if it has Deno/Supabase; else the generic npm ci auto-setup). Agent internet Off. (Skip if you'll only use Cyrus.)
  2. Linear ↔ GitHub — Linear → Settings → Integrations → GitHub → connect the repo, and in the status-automation section map PR opened → In Review and merged → Done (both — the second half is what B-Unit was missing).

docs.title: Gotchas baked in (learned the hard way on B-Unit — don't rediscover)
docs.text:
• Orthogonal dispatch: delegate issues that touch different files. Parallel agents on overlapping files → merge conflicts (and a migration-number collision). Slice by subsystem.
  • New migrations use timestamped names (supabase migration new) so parallel agents can't collide on 00NN. Never rename/renumber already-applied migrations — it desyncs prod's history table and needs a supabase migration repair.
  • Prod migrations from CI need a POOLER url (*.pooler.supabase.com, IPv4). GitHub runners are IPv4-only; the direct db.<ref>.supabase.co host is IPv6-only → unreachable. Don't buy the IPv4 add-on.
  • Agents propose, humans apply. Agents open migration PRs; a human clicks the deploy button. Never give agents autonomous prod-DB write access (live app / real data).
  • Per-tool MCP: delegating in Cyrus/Codex is automatic for its issue; a hands-on Claude Code session only touches Linear when you tell it to.

docs.title: Reference docs (the full detail behind each piece)
docs.text:
• Per-repo operating manual: <repo>/docs/linear-workflow.md (the portable template).
  • Cyrus internals/ops: [[cyrus-claude-code-linear-agent-hermes]].
  • Codex Cloud env drift: ~/dev/bunit/docs/solutions/integration-issues/codex-cloud-setup-script-drift-no-pr.md.
  • Migration history repair + pooler-in-CI: ~/dev/bunit/docs/solutions/… (pending — task spawned 2026-07-07).

docs.title: meeting-capture
docs.text: Purpose: drain Persik meet Name: queue → append verbatim notes to the daily journal and add a dated cross-link on Vault/References/{Name}.md. Full prose stays in the daily note — person notes are an index only. Trigger: folded into journal-capture step 9 (same hourly Cowork tick) · on demand "flush meeting" · "meeting capture". Role: COO. Output: appended blocks in Vault/YYYY-MM-DD.md; ## Meetings line on person note; journal_inbox rows kind=meeting marked applied. Model: Haiku 4.5 — mechanical only (fetch queue → append daily → one index line → PATCH). No summarization.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
1. Load .secrets/newfin-cron.env: CRON_SECRET, NEWFIN_API_BASE.
  2. GET $NEWFIN_API_BASE/api/cron/journal-inbox?status=pending&kind=meeting&limit=20 with Bearer CRON_SECRET.
  3. If empty → stop (report 0). Short-circuit before git work (same as journal-capture).
  4. Lock-contention defer — same rules as journal-capture § 3b: if Jackie-OS git lock persists after wait → abort cleanly; entries stay pending.
  5. git pull Jackie-OS — only when queue is non-empty.
  6. For each entry (meeting_person, text, journal_date, captured_at):

  7. Daily append — same format as journal-capture on Vault/{journal_date}.md:

    ---

**HH:MM** (Telegram · [[{Person}]])

{verbatim text}

    Use Europe/Warsaw wall time from captured_at. Create the daily from Vault/Templates/Journal entry.md if missing. - Person index — Vault/References/{Person}.md where {Person} is title-cased meeting_person (e.g. David, Andriy Kusyy): - File missing — create from Vault/Templates/Person.md, add # {Person} heading under frontmatter. - Append only under ## Meetings (create section at file end if absent):

    - YYYY-MM-DD — [[YYYY-MM-DD]] — {first ~80 chars of text, ellipsis if truncated}
    • Skip the line if an identical YYYY-MM-DD — [[YYYY-MM-DD]] entry already exists for that person.
    • Never edit biography or prior meeting lines — index append only.
    • Person enrich (6b) — if step 6 created a new References/{Person}.md (file did not exist before this entry), run person-enrich for that name in the same session before commit. Skip if file already existed (Sergei may have hand-written ## My relationship).
    • One git commit per run if any files changed: Meeting capture YYYY-MM-DD (+N entries).
    • PATCH $NEWFIN_API_BASE/api/cron/journal-inbox/{id} {"status":"applied"} for each row.
    • Report: N entries, dates touched, people indexed.

docs.title: Persik capture (Newfin side)
docs.text: Owner DM prefix: meet {Name}: {notes} (also meet {Name} — …). Routes to journal_inbox kind=meeting with meeting_person. Not finance intent, not a clip.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Daily is canonical — never duplicate full meeting body on the person note.
  • Append-only on dailies and person ## Meetings — same discipline as journal-capture.
  • Credentials in text → do not write; PATCH applied and flag in report.
  • Spouse/group never enqueue meetings.
  • Yield on lock — defer to next hour; never clear Jackie-OS git locks.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Requires Newfin migration journal_inbox_meeting (kind=meeting, meeting_person column) and Persik meet Name: router deployed. Runs on the same Mac Cowork host as journal-capture.

Hub note for humans: [[Meetings]].

Person notes: public web data via person-enrich; your words stay in dailies + ## My relationship.

docs.title: morning-brief
docs.text: Purpose: daily COO brief — yesterday, top 3, projects/open loops, code repos, calendar, inbox, thesis check — plus folded telegram-sweep (step 0), trade-digest (step 0b), and daily-linking (after brief). Trigger: scheduled daily 07:30, or "morning brief" / "daily brief". Role: COO. Output: Vault/Briefs/YYYY-MM-DD brief.md. (Vault/Briefs/ = Claude's briefs; Obsidian daily notes = Sergei's journal — separate things.)

docs.title: Wake-race guard — run BEFORE anything else
docs.text:
This task is scheduled 07:30 but usually fires in catch-up the moment the laptop wakes (often 08:00–09:00). At that moment Obsidian Sync may still be pulling overnight/phone edits to disk and git hasn't fetched — so the vault on disk is stale and a brief generated now silently misses real work. See CHANGELOG for the 2026-06-14 wake-race incident.

  1. Telegram sweep (folded) — follow telegram-sweep before sync/brief so overnight clips land in the vault and the thesis check sees them. Short-circuit if the clip queue is empty (no git pull).

Git — native only (Cowork). First line of the run — clear locks from any previous Cowork session. Never git pull / git commit Jackie-OS in Cowork bash. 

osascript -e 'do shell script "/Users/jackie/Jackie-OS/System/scripts/jackie-os-git-native.sh sweep --force"'
See project-sync § Git lock hygiene.

0b. Trade digest (folded) — drain Persik closed-trade learnings into [[Trading playbook]] (vault narrative only — not where hard rules live; those stay in Newfin profile_facts / advisor_memory). Mechanical append; no interpretation. 1. Load .secrets/newfin-cron.env: CRON_SECRET, NEWFIN_API_BASE. 2. GET $NEWFIN_API_BASE/api/cron/journal-inbox?kind=trade_digest&status=pending&limit=20 with Bearer CRON_SECRET. 3. If empty → skip (no git work for this step). 4. osascript -e 'do shell script "/Users/jackie/Jackie-OS/System/scripts/jackie-os-git-native.sh pull"' — only if not already pulled this run. 5. For each row, append to Vault/Trading playbook.md (create from template below if missing):

  ```
  ---

  **YYYY-MM-DD** (trade close)

  {verbatim text from inbox row}
  ```

  Use `captured_at` date (Europe/Warsaw) for the heading.
  1. PATCH …/journal-inbox/{id} {"status":"applied"} for each row.
  2. If the playbook changed: stage for the single end-of-run commit (do not commit here). Report N in the session log.
  3. Settle check. Stamp the real wall-clock time (date). Stat the active project notes (Vault/{Newfin,Jackie OS,Rodyna,Draw,Peaches Beauty}.md), today's + yesterday's daily notes, and Vault/hot.md. Wait ~90 s, re-stat. If any mtime changed, the vault is still syncing → wait another ~90 s and repeat (cap ~5 min). Proceed only once two consecutive stats match (sync quiesced), or the cap is hit — in which case say so in the brief ("generated before vault sync settled — verify").
  4. Fetch. Run project-sync's git fetch (step 0) so origin refs are as fresh as the machine allows.
  5. Never hardcode the run time. The Log section uses the real fire time from step 1, not "07:30".

docs.title: Prompt caching — the stable prefix
docs.text: The "Read first" block (CLAUDE.md, Vault/CLAUDE.md, Vault/Home.md) is stable across runs — same bytes every day until those files are edited. When the runner supports prompt caching (Anthropic cache_control: ephemeral, Gemini cachedContent), tag that block to land in cache; on a typical morning brief it's the dominant share of input tokens. hot.md and yesterday's brief change daily and are not cache candidates. Pinning the prefix typically cuts daily-brief input cost by ~50–80%.

docs.title: Source of truth — notes over cache
docs.text:
Project status in the brief is derived from each active project note's ## Status — read it in step 2 using the rolling work window below, not only the newest block. hot.md and yesterday's brief are orientation only; never let them author the project narrative. If a note's Status records shipped/pushed work that the local git number doesn't reflect (common: pushed from another machine, sandbox can't fetch), report the note's account and flag the git delta as unverified — do not downgrade a project to "blocked/stalled/carried" when its own note says otherwise.

Ops kanban (Vault/Ops/Tasks/, Vault/Ops/Plans/) is the forward-looking execution layer — what Sergei (or agents on wrap-up) marked todo · doing · blocked · active on the boards. Read it in § Ops board after project-sync, before Today + Projects. When Ops and vault Status disagree on blocked/next, Ops blocked tasks win for icons and Attention; Status Next: still leads Projects prose unless every open task is blocked.

docs.title: Ops board (kanban)
docs.text:
When: Vault/Ops/Bases/Work.base exists (skip section if missing) or any registry row is tracker: linear.

Two task sources, by registry tracker flag (see registry § Tracker switch):

  • tracker: bases (default, every non-migrated project) — read all notes in Vault/Ops/Tasks/*.md and Vault/Ops/Plans/*.md, parse frontmatter: project, status, priority, title, blocked, kind. (Unchanged.)
  • tracker: linear (B-Unit today) — do not read that project's Ops Bases cards; its tasks come from Linear. Step 0's project-sync already ran System/scripts/linear-fetch.py --project "<name>" (§ C2) — reuse that JSON, or re-run it (cheap, read-only). Map: open/top_candidates → Todo/Doing candidates (Linear statusType started = doing, unstarted = todo, backlog = backlog); recently_done → Since last brief · Work; a top_candidates item whose body marks it blocked → Blocked. Linear priority 1/2 ≈ P1/P2 for Top-3 ranking (priorityName in the JSON). If the fetch returned an error field (missing key / API hiccup), note "Linear unread — {reason}" in Log and fall back to that project's vault ## Status Next: only.

Aggregate:

Bucket Rule Doing status: doing — global count; list by project (priority asc) Blocked status: blocked — list title + project; include blocked: field when set Todo P1 status: todo and priority: 1 — Top 3 candidates Active plans status: active in Plans/ — one line per project if any WIP flag >3 doing globally → ⚠️ in Log + mention in Today or Attention

Feed into brief sections:

  1. Today · Top 3 — prefer, in order: 🔴 inbox · doing tasks (finish before starting new) · todo P1/P2 · calendar-hard commitments · vault Status Next:. Max one slot per project when possible.
  2. Projects icons — start from vault lane / Status Blocked:, then adjust:
  3. 🔴 if any blocked task on board for that project or Status blocked
  4. 🟡 if doing tasks exist but nothing blocked
  5. 🟢 default when on track
  6. Append · {N} blocked when N>0 (short — titles live in Attention)
  7. Attention — Ops · blocked subsection when any blocked tasks: up to 5 bullets **{Project}** — {title} (+ reason from blocked: field). Heads-up if lane: active but tasks blocked (Peaches pattern).
  8. Projects line — still Next from Status; may add · doing: {title} when exactly one doing task (optional, keep one line).

Do not duplicate full kanban in the brief — counts + blocked titles + doing list only. Done tasks/plans live in Since last brief · Work via Status/git, not Progress table.

docs.title: Rolling work window (heavy sprint days)
docs.text:
Calendar midnight alone loses work that spans evenings and overnight sessions (common on Rodyna/Newfin sprints). Use a rolling window ending at brief generation time:

  1. Window start — the earlier of: (a) timestamp in yesterday's brief ## Log first line (real fire time), or (b) 24 hours before brief generation (Europe/Warsaw). Never use calendar "yesterday 00:00" alone.
  2. Status prepends — for each active project, read every *YYYY-MM-DD …* block under ## Status whose stamp falls in the window. Do not stop at the newest block.
  3. merge-poll blocks — include every (merge-poll) entry in the window (they may list 25 commits with a total count when truncated).
  4. Git delta — for each registry git row: git log <window-start-ish>..origin/<branch> --oneline (also compare to lastSyncedSha from project-sync-state.json; use whichever baseline catches more commits). If ≥15 commits or ≥3 distinct themes for a repo, Yesterday · Work and Projects MUST use themed bullets (3–5 max per project), not one PR-centric paragraph.
  5. Theme buckets (suggested labels): UI/miniapp, ingest/bot, catalog/data, perf/infra, docs/plans. Latest ## Status Next/Blocked still sets what's open today.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
Read first: Vault/hot.md (session cache — fastest orientation), then CLAUDE.md (root), Vault/CLAUDE.md, yesterday's brief. Do not read Home.md for ops — drill into project notes ## Status per ops-board § Agent orientation.

  1. Project sync (sole owner) — follow project-sync so all projects (code repos, Projects/*/STATUS.md, vault notes) reflect overnight work in any tool — write/stage only; do not commit yet. This is the only morning task that syncs the vault. No freshness gate: always run. If git fetch can't reach GitHub (sandbox), honor project-sync's stale-origin rule — never regress a project whose note records newer pushed work. 0c. Ops board scan — when Vault/Ops/Bases/Work.base exists, run § Ops board aggregation (Tasks + Plans frontmatter). Hold results for steps 2–4.
  2. Since last brief — two parts: work, then life.
  3. Work — follow Rolling work window: all Status prepends + merge-poll entries + git log in the window. Per active project, lead with what shipped as a short narrative; on sprint days use themed bullets (3–5 max), not one latest-PR paragraph. Route Shipped: lines from Status prepends here. Carry forward unfinished items. Respond explicitly to anything Sergei wrote in {curly brackets}.
  4. Life — read yesterday's daily note Vault/{yesterday YYYY-MM-DD}.md (and skim the last 2–3 days + today's note for continuity). Synthesize, don't just recap (Sergei has opted into depth here): the emotional/experiential arc, what genuinely seemed to matter, threads that recur across recent days, and tensions or shifts worth noticing. Close with one gentle observation or open question offered for his reflection — tentative, in service of his own thinking, never a clinical verdict. Always link → [[yesterday's date]]. Hard rules: skip anything tagged #private (or in a private note) entirely — don't read, quote, or synthesize it; never edit the journal; the deep cross-week patterns stay in the weekly review (this is the daily, lighter touch). If yesterday's note is empty/missing, say so in one line and link today's [[date]].
  5. Today — propose Top 3 using Ops board candidates + open loops and calendar; include Calendar events (or "none"); fold Review reminders here when week/month artifact missing (step 11 rules). Sergei overrides. If doing >3 globally, add one line: "WIP high — {N} in flight."

Calendar (required before glance + Today): fetch all timed events today in Europe/Warsaw — including evening — from Google Calendar (Cowork connector) or macOS Calendar.app (Google-synced calendars). Count every timed event; do not write no events without a live fetch. Family/shared calendars matter (e.g. Сім'я). Resending Telegram (brief-to-telegram.py) does not refresh calendar — patch the vault brief first if events were missed at generation.

Weather / location (glance line): run ~/.hermes/scripts/google-life-fetch.py (or read its output in the VPS prompt). It infers current city from recent journals + briefs + hot.md (e.g. Italy trip → Bologna weather, not Warsaw). Override with BRIEF_WEATHER_CITY=bologna in .secrets/google-oauth.env if inference is wrong. The 🌤️ line must use the inferred city — never default to Warsaw when vault says Sergei is traveling. 3. Projects — apply the rolling work window for context but write forward-looking only: icon from Ops board rules + Next/Blocked from Status + inline (main sha) per active project. On sprint days add Shipped → see Since last brief · Work — do not repeat ship narrative. Append git ⚠ under a project when dirty / behind / origin-unverified (replaces the old code-repos table). Dormant rows only if blockers in vault Status. [[Jackie OS]] line = system/engineering only (skills, workflows, infra) — not vault content. 4. Attention — Ops · blocked first when step 0c found blocked tasks (≤5 bullets); then Inbox action items (🔴/🟡 only + one heads-up line); then Read queue (count + 3 oldest unread → [[Read Later]]). Regenerate Vault/Read Later.md from the clippings scan (same rules as old step 7). Omit subsections when empty. 5. Signal — Knowledge (24h vault additions: count + 2–3 highlights) + Thesis check (contradictions only; omit subsection when none). Skip #private. Skill improvements (removable nudge): count open rows in skill-feedback; if ≥1, add one line — 🛠️ N skill improvement(s) pending — say "improve skills" to review diffs; omit the line entirely when zero. 6. Log (vault only) — fire time, sync, Telegram delivery results. Not included in the DM body.

Review rules (for Today section): nudge period closes only when Sergei's period note is still missing:

- **Week close** — if today is **Saturday, Sunday, or Tuesday** and vault root `YYYY-Www.md` for the **current ISO week** does **not** exist: remind — read `[[YYYY-Www brief]]` (Sun auto) · run **`weekly review`** to write your week.
- **Month close** — if today is in the **last 3 calendar days of the month** OR **days 1–3 of a new month**, and prior month's `YYYY-Mmm.md` (e.g. `2026-M06.md`) is missing: if brief exists, remind read + **`monthly review`**; else **`monthly review`** to generate brief first.
- **Year close** — if today is **Jan 1–7** and prior year's `YYYY.md` is missing: if `Briefs/YYYY brief.md` exists, remind read + **`yearly review`**; else generate brief first. Optional soft line Dec 26–31: "year close soon."
- If none apply → omit review lines in Today (don't nag).

💰 Trading learnings (vault archive). Step 0b drains trade_digest closes into [[Trading playbook]] — optional mention under Signal when step 0b applied rows overnight.

docs.title: Output format
docs.text:
Write the brief to the template below. It is built to be scanned in 15 seconds, then read in 2 minutes — a TL;DR + at-a-glance line up top, then short sections. Telegram DM is the phone reader (brief-to-telegram.py): plain prose beats meta (no "rolling window", "Shipped:", or cross-refs like "see Since last brief").

Voice rules:

  • TL;DR — max ~25 words. Outcome + today's lever. No commit counts or PR numbers.
  • At a glance — one plain line with · separators. No backticks. Weather · calendar · inbox count · top lever.
  • Today — numbered list; each item = bold verb phrase + one short why.
  • Since last brief · Work — lead with what changed for the user, not git stats. Sprint days: 4 bullets max per project, plain labels (App, Ingest, etc.). Separate projects as their own short blocks — don't merge Newfin + Jackie OS into one line.
  • Projects — one line each: icon + name + Next only. Icon from Ops blocked/doing rules. Optional · N blocked suffix. No sha, no "Shipped → see…" footnotes.
  • Attention — Ops · blocked first (kanban), then inbox. One heads-up paragraph for non-action items.
  • Signal — 2–3 lines max unless thesis moved.

Status icon legend (use consistently):

  • 🟢 on track / shipped · 🟡 needs attention / in progress · 🔴 blocked · ⚪ dormant

Section headings: Scan (TL;DR + bar inline) · Today · Since last brief (Work · Life) · Projects · Attention · Signal · Log (vault only).

docs.title: Template
docs.text:
---
categories:
  - "[[Briefs]]"
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---

# 🗓️ YYYY-MM-DD · {Weekday} — Daily brief

> ⚡ **TL;DR** — {max ~25 words: main outcome + today's lever.}

🌤️ {city} {hi}/{lo}°C {conditions} · 📅 {N events or "no events"} · 📥 {N inbox} · 🎯 {top lever}

---

## Today

1. **{Action}** — {one short line.}
2. **{Action}** — {one short line.}
3. **{Action}** — {one short line.}

**Calendar** — {timed events or "clear."}

**Review** — {week/month nudge if artifact missing; else omit.}

---

## Since last brief

### Work

**{Project}** — {one-line lead, then 2–4 bullets on sprint days.}

**{Project}** — {short block; separate per project.}

### Life · {yesterday YYYY-MM-DD}

{2–4 sentences + one gentle question. Skip #private.}

---

## Projects

- 🟢 **{Project}** — {Next only; one line.}
- ⚪ **{Dormant}** — {only if blocker.}

---

## Attention

**Ops · blocked**

- 🔴 **{Project}** — {task title}{ — reason if `blocked:` set.}
- …

**Inbox**

- 🔴 **{item}** — {action.}
- 🟡 **{item}** — {action.}

Heads-up: {one short paragraph for non-action items.}

**Read queue** — {N unread. Oldest titles + ages. "+M in Read Later." Omit if zero.}

---

## Signal

- {1–2 knowledge highlights}
- **Thesis** — {movement or "no movement."}
- 🛠️ {N skill improvement(s) pending — "improve skills" to review; omit line when zero.}

---

## Log

- {HH:MM} — brief generated; {settle state}; ops: {N doing}, {M blocked}.
- {HH:MM} — Telegram summary + HTML attach {ok|failed}; coo-cache {ok|skipped}.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Wikilinks only; YYYY-MM-DD; Russian/English mix fine; never edit journals; never rename notes. Emoji are structural signposts — one per section heading + the status legend; don't pepper them through prose. Keep the at-a-glance bar to one line. After writing the brief, deliver it to Telegram first (§ Telegram delivery — decoupled from git), then add today's row to the [[Daily]] index (daily note + brief links, newest first — the daily-note link may be unresolved until Sergei writes it) and the brief to [[Briefs]] under Daily. Run daily linking (§ Daily linking) before the commit. End with one native commit for the whole run (project-sync + brief + indexes + trade-digest + links.md): 

osascript -e 'do shell script "/Users/jackie/Jackie-OS/System/scripts/jackie-os-git-native.sh commit Daily brief YYYY-MM-DD"'
Adjust the message for clip/link counts when useful. Never git commit in Cowork bash. If commit fails (live non-empty lock from another writer), log git: deferred in Log — brief delivery already happened; do not retry or call allow_cowork_file_delete.

docs.title: Telegram delivery (Persik — one message: caption + HTML file)
docs.text: Decoupled from git — deliver FIRST. After writing Vault/Briefs/YYYY-MM-DD brief.md, before git commit.

docs.title: 1. Send brief (single message)
docs.text:
Mac (has telegram.env): 

python3 System/coo/brief-to-telegram.py "Vault/Briefs/$(date +%F) brief.md"

VPS (no bot token — uses Newfin API): 

python3 ~/.hermes/scripts/brief-deliver-via-cron.py "Vault/Briefs/$(date +%F) brief.md"
Requires POST /api/cron/coo-brief-deliver on Newfin (sendDocument + coo cache). morning-brief-vps.py calls this automatically after generation.

  • Load .secrets/telegram.env (Mac only): TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_USER_ID. Missing → log skip, continue to commit.
  • One sendDocument: HTML file + caption = 🗓️ date · ⚡ outcome only (TL;DR before Today:) · one caption row per glance segment (weather, calendar, inbox — no 🎯 lever) · 🎯 Top 3 short labels. No repeated levers across lines.
  • Tap the file to read the full styled brief. Log excluded. stdout JSON: { "ok", "message_id", "caption", "filename", "html_bytes" }.

docs.title: 2. COO cache (silent — no second DM)
docs.text:
Load .secrets/newfin-cron.env: CRON_SECRET, NEWFIN_API_BASE.

Build digest_html from Scan + Today + Projects sections (~3500 char cap, minimal HTML: <b>, <br>).

curl -s --max-time 30 -X POST "${NEWFIN_API_BASE}/api/cron/coo-push" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${CRON_SECRET}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"kind\":\"daily\",\"period_key\":\"$(date +%F)\",\"digest_html\":\"...\",\"notify\":false}"

Missing env / 404 → log once, continue. Powers Persik /day and Ask — not a user notification.

docs.title: 3. Log + commit
docs.text:
Append to brief Log: Telegram summary + HTML attach {ok|failed}; coo-cache {ok|skipped}. Then run daily linking (§ Daily linking), then one end-of-run commit per Rules (not here).

Weekly review still uses coo-push with default notify: true (loud digest). Daily uses notify: false after Telegram delivery.

docs.title: Life context ingest (planned — Newfin Phase C2)
docs.text:
When Newfin life_context_cache ships, add after the Telegram delivery step above:

  1. Build JSON from vault: Vault/hot.md (or hot block), today's Vault/YYYY-MM-DD.md excerpt (~1–2k chars), active projects from registry / project notes ([{ "name", "status" }]).
  2. POST $NEWFIN_API_BASE/api/cron/life-context-ingest with same Bearer + body: 
    { "hot_md": "…", "journal_excerpt": "…", "active_projects": [] }
  3. Missing endpoint or 404 → log once "life-context-ingest skipped — Newfin C2 not deployed" and continue.

Until C2a is merged, do not call this endpoint.

docs.title: Daily linking (folded)
docs.text:
After Telegram delivery and coo-cache (brief body and Log are already written):

  1. Follow daily-linking exactly — auto-link cap 5, write Vault/Briefs/YYYY-MM-DD links.md. Do not commit — morning-brief owns the single end-of-run commit.
  2. Log one line in the brief Log: daily-linking: N auto-linked, M for review (or empty day).
  3. One native commit via jackie-os-git-native.sh commit (see Rules). Post-commit sweep is inside the script.

Run linking after the brief file exists; linking does not edit the brief body. Haiku is fine for linking (per daily-linking skill). Retired Cowork tasks: see CHANGELOG.

docs.title: Knowledge candidates (folded)
docs.text:
During Attention, surface up to 3 clips ready for Knowledge action:

  • knowledge_state: candidate
  • read/rated 4-5 clips missing knowledge_state
  • repeated sources that point to the same Knowledge subtopic

Do not integrate candidates automatically. Use one-click choices like append to Knowledge, ignore, or ask me later. If Sergei approves append, follow knowledge-integration.

During Signal, include 1-2 Knowledge highlights or open questions from relevant Vault/Knowledge/*.md when they help today's projects or decisions.

docs.title: multi-agent-run
docs.text:
Trigger: Sergei says "run wave N" / "multi-agent run" / "use the workflow for this", or a plan doc exists with ≥5 independent, well-specified tasks. Requires explicit owner opt-in — never launch a Workflow for inferred scale.

Proven shape (2026-07-08 Wave 1: 11 tasks, 22 agents, 13 min, 9/11 first-pass): spec → dry-run verify → Workflow(worker→verifier per task) → lead merges → gates → wrap-up.

docs.title: Phase 0 — Spec (before any agents)
docs.text:
1. Every task gets: unique ID, repo, exact file paths, concrete steps, acceptance criteria a verifier can check against a diff, effort, dependencies. One task = one worker with zero follow-up questions.
  2. Separate owner-manual tasks (secrets, prod migrations, product decisions) into an OM-* list — never delegate those.
  3. Dry-run verify the spec itself: one read-only agent per repo checks every path exists and every claim is true. (Wave 1: this caught 5 spec errors — wrong dirs, a client-side env var listed as server-required, already-existing glossary terms.)

docs.title: Phase 1 — The Workflow script
docs.text:
Shape (see System/plans/2026-07-08-worker-handoff-plan.md § Appendix for a full example):

pipeline(IDS,
  id => agent(workPrompt(id), { label: `work:${id}`, phase: 'Work', model: 'sonnet' }),
  (report, id) => agent(verifyPrompt(id, report), { label: `verify:${id}`, phase: 'Verify',
    model: 'sonnet', schema: { type:'object', properties:{ pass:{type:'boolean'}, reasons:{type:'array', items:{type:'string'}} }, required:['pass'] } })
    .then(v => ({ id, ...v })))

Hard-won rules:

  • Worktree isolation per worker, via explicit git command in the prompt — git -C <repo> worktree add <ABSOLUTE scratchpad path>/wt-<id> -b agents/<id> <base>. Workers commit on their branch, never push. Use absolute literal paths in prompts — template variables get mangled by workers (Wave 1: ${scratchDir} came through as undefined/ for 10 of 11 workers; work survived only because branches share the repo's object store). The Workflow tool's built-in isolation:'worktree' only covers the session repo — explicit git worktrees work across repos.
  • Verifier gets a schema (pass: boolean + reasons), never string-match verdicts (Wave 1 bug: 4 verifiers wrote prose before "PASS" and were miscounted as FAIL). Verifier checks the branch diff, treats the worker's report as untrusted, and also confirms nothing out-of-scope changed.
  • Standard RULES block in every worker prompt: read repo CLAUDE.md; never touch draw / Vault journals / private notes / .obsidian / .secrets; wikilinks in vault docs; git status first — dirty-from-another-writer → STOP and report.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Lead closes (never delegate this)
docs.text:
1. Read verdicts yourself — verifiers err strict (line-number nits) and loose (phantom "file missing" claims); spot-check disputed facts before rerunning anything.
  2. Merge PASS branches sequentially (git merge --no-ff); overlapping-file conflicts are expected and small — keep both edits. Fix trivial verifier nits at merge time instead of re-running the worker.
  3. Re-run true failures as single Agent calls with the corrected instruction (cheaper than workflow resume for 1-2 tasks).
  4. Gates before push: repo checks (newfin: typecheck + tests; jackie-os: link-check). Then push.
  5. Cleanup: git worktree remove each + git worktree prune + delete agents/* branches. Check for stray undefined/ dirs inside repos.
  6. Wrap-up per wrap-up: roadmap reconcile (plan row → wave status), vault Status prepend, brief Log, push.

docs.title: When NOT to use
docs.text: <5 tasks, tasks with sequential dependencies on each other's output, exploratory/unspecified work (spec it first), or anything touching prod state (that's an OM item).

docs.title: new-project
docs.text: Purpose: one-shot onboarding for a new project — code repo OR non-code — into Jackie OS, so everything (registry, vault note, indexes, learnings, sync coverage) is wired before real work starts. The agent does all the wiring; for code repos there is zero manual setup if the read PAT is scoped to all your repos (see § One-time prerequisite). Trigger: "new project", "new code project", "new non-code project", "register project", "I created a repo", "set up project X" — or the agent detects an unregistered project Sergei is starting. Role: COO + CTO setup. Output: registry row; Vault/{Title}.md note; Projects.md / Home.md index links; (code) repo bridge + learnings catalog + poller registration; (non-code) Projects/{Name}/ folder; one commit.

docs.title: Step 0 — classify
docs.text:
Ask (or infer): project name / title, type — code (its own git repo) or non-code (lives inside jackie-os) — active?, and for code: GitHub remote (owner/repo), local path, default branch (main), owned or shared?.

Then run the matching path. Both end with a single git commit in jackie-os.

docs.title: Path A — code project (own git repo)
docs.text:
Ownership gate: if the remote owner isn't Sergei's account (e.g. AleannLab/…) or he says it's shared, mark the registry row 🤝 read-only, and skip steps 4–6 (repo bridge, design system, code-repo commit) — Jackie-OS reads a shared repo into the vault but never writes to it and never polls it with the PAT.

  1. Registry — add a git row to System/project-registry.md: paths, branch, GitHub remote, mirror if any, Roadmap index (plans/roadmap-index.md — required for owned repos; — for shared 🤝).
  2. Vault note + indexes — Vault/{Title}.md (frontmatter [[Projects]], stub, empty ## Status); add wikilink to Vault/Projects.md; if Active, add to Vault/Home.md Active list.
  3. Learnings — Vault/Agent-Learnings/{Title} learnings.md from the [[Newfin learnings]] template; add a row to Vault/Agent-Learnings/Index.md.
  4. Repo bridge (in the code repo — owned only): copy System/templates/JACKIE-OS-bridge.md → docs/JACKIE-OS.md (fill KEY, vault note, branch); scaffold docs/solutions/README.md if missing; add the Vault sync paragraph to the repo's CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md (point to docs/JACKIE-OS.md).
  5. Plans scaffold (owned code repos only — skip 🤝 shared):
  6. Create plans/ from System/templates/plans/: README.md, roadmap-index.md, future-improvements.md, archive/README.md.
  7. Replace placeholders: {PROJECT} = display name, {DATE} = today YYYY-MM-DD, {INITIAL_SHA} = git rev-parse --short HEAD (or 0000000 before first commit).
  8. Append System/templates/CLAUDE-planning-section.md to CLAUDE.md (create ## Planning if missing). Mirror one line in AGENTS.md if present.
  9. In vault note ## Status stub, link plans/roadmap-index.md as the forward-work surface.
  10. Do not copy Newfin/Rodyna-specific archives — empty plans/archive/ except README.
  11. Design system (owned code repos — skip API-only / CLI-only / shared 🤝):
  12. When: Step 0 expects a user-facing UI, or the repo already has a frontend package (web/, miniapp/, frontend/, apps/*/web, or a subdir with react/vue/svelte in package.json). If Sergei says "no UI", skip.
  13. Doc path (first match):
    • miniapp/ → miniapp/docs/design-memory.md
    • web/ at repo root → docs/design-system.md (token source: web/src/styles/globals.css or project's token file)
    • other UI package {pkg}/ → {pkg}/docs/design-memory.md
    • UI planned but not scaffolded yet → docs/design-system.md at repo root ({UI_PACKAGE} = TBD, {TOKEN_SOURCE} = TBD)
  14. Copy System/templates/design-system.md; replace {PROJECT}, {UI_PACKAGE}, {TOKEN_SOURCE}. Template includes YAML frontmatter (DESIGN.md format) + prose; fill anchor token values from the token CSS file. Do not overwrite an existing design doc — merge or skip if one is already canonical (e.g. Newfin docs/design-system.md, Rodyna miniapp/docs/design-memory.md).
  15. Add design:lint to the repo root package.json (or UI workspace package.json if no root scripts): "design:lint": "npx -p @google/design.md@0.3.0 designmd lint <DESIGN_DOC_REL>" — path matches the doc from the bullet above.
  16. Append the UI section from System/templates/AGENTS-design-section.md to AGENTS.md and/or CLAUDE.md (replace {UI_PACKAGE}, {DESIGN_DOC_REL}). Skip if an equivalent section already points at the design doc.
  17. Page-load benchmark (FF 003): copy System/templates/benchmark-page-load.md into the repo (path per layout — e.g. docs/performance.md or {UI_PACKAGE}/docs/performance.md). Scaffold benchmark script from Newfin (server/src/scripts/benchmark-page-load.ts) or Rodyna (miniapp/scripts/benchmark-page-load.ts) pattern. Add npm run benchmark:pages + Definition of done line: new screen → add to benchmark; all routes <50ms p50 warm.
  18. Optional later (not required at onboarding): npm run setup:ui + mock API + deep links — see Rodyna miniapp/README.md § Plain-browser design work.
  19. Commit in the code repo — bridge + solutions + plans/ + design doc + AGENTS/CLAUDE blurbs in one PR or push.
  20. Poller — nothing to do. The merge-poll is registry-driven (.github/scripts/merge_poll.py reads project-registry.md), so adding the row in A1 already puts the repo under the intraday poll (owned sc-jackie/*, Active, not shared). (If the JACKIE_OS_READ_PAT is scoped to selected repos rather than all, add this repo to the PAT — avoid that entirely with an all-repos read PAT.)
  21. Project-sync — run project-sync; prepend the vault ## Status stub; refresh hot.md if Active.
  22. Linear + agents (optional, owned repos) — to put the repo on the Linear board with Cyrus/Codex delegation, run linear-project-rollout next. The 3 label groups (Pipeline/Stage/Type) are workspace-shared, so there's nothing to create — just a project + IDs swap.

docs.title: Path B — non-code project (lives inside jackie-os)
docs.text:
No GitHub repo, no bridge, no Action, no secret — the work is in the vault, so the commit is the sync.

  1. Folder — create Projects/{Name}/ for working files; add Projects/{Name}/STATUS.md only if you want a status-file mirror.
  2. Plans scaffold — create Projects/{Name}/plans/ from System/templates/projects-plans/: README.md, roadmap-index.md, future-improvements.md, archive/README.md. Replace {PROJECT}, {VAULT_NOTE}, {DATE}. Registry Roadmap index → Projects/{Name}/plans/roadmap-index.md.
  3. Registry — add a vault row (or status-file row if you made a STATUS.md) to System/project-registry.md with Roadmap index path from step 2.
  4. Vault note + indexes — Vault/{Title}.md (frontmatter, stub, empty ## Status); wikilink in Vault/Projects.md; Active list in Home.md if active. Link Projects/{Name}/plans/roadmap-index.md in the stub.
  5. Commit — git commit jackie-os. Done — morning-brief + wrap-up track it from here.

docs.title: One-time prerequisite (Sergei, once ever — not per project)
docs.text:
For code repos to get intraday merge-poll coverage, jackie-os needs one secret: - Create one fine-grained PAT → Contents: Read, scoped to All repositories under sc-jackie (so every future repo is auto-covered — no per-project secret work). - Add it to jackie-os → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → JACKIE_OS_READ_PAT.

Skip this and code repos still sync daily via the 07:30 morning-brief — you just lose the intraday entry. Non-code projects need nothing.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• [ ] project-sync shows the new row without errors (path exists, or flagged skip).
  • [ ] Vault note + index links exist; (code) learnings catalog + Index.md row present.
  • [ ] Code, owned: docs/JACKIE-OS.md + docs/solutions/README.md + plans/ (roadmap-index, future-improvements, README, archive/) committed in the repo; CLAUDE.md Planning section; repo in merge poll via registry. UI repos: design doc + AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md UI section + page-load benchmark (npm run benchmark:pages, <50ms p50 DoD) — or documented skip reason. Shared (🤝): confirm NOTHING was written/pushed to the repo, Roadmap index = —, and it's NOT in merge_poll.py.
  • [ ] Non-code: Projects/{Name}/ + Projects/{Name}/plans/ + vault note committed; no repo/bridge/Action created.

docs.title: Workflows that pick up automatically (after onboarding)
docs.text:
Workflow How it finds the project project-sync System/project-registry.md morning-brief (07:30) Active registry rows → rich vault Status daily (authoritative sync) merge-poll (~3h) .github/scripts/merge_poll.py REPOS — code repos only, thin intraday entry wrap-up project-sync all rows; § Catalog cleanup on plans/ when code ships hot.md Active project one-liners from vault Status weekly-review Vault notes + week dailies jos-compound Run in-session after a non-trivial fix (not automated) → repo docs/solutions/ + [[agent-learnings-index]] row Planning loop plans/roadmap-index.md → dated plan → ship → archive + catalog cleanup (wrap-up)

Do not auto-wire: Cursor automations (none exist), Peaches-style Cowork one-offs, Hermes VPS.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Push the code repo before expecting project-sync to see commits.
  • Nested repo inside Jackie-OS (Rodyna pattern): ensure the clone is in jackie-os .gitignore; registry path points at the clone.
  • Never duplicate full docs/solutions/ bodies into the vault — index rows only.
  • Shared / external / contribute-only repos (🤝, e.g. AleannLab/draw): registry + vault note + learnings catalog are OK (Jackie-OS side only). Never write a bridge/docs/solutions//CLAUDE.md into the repo, never push/PR to it, never add it to merge_poll.py. Sync is read-only via morning-brief. (Registry Write policy — 2026-06-13 draw leak.)

docs.title: ops-board
docs.text: Purpose: Trello-style tracking — one card = one note. Per-project kanbans and roll-up boards read the same Vault/Ops/Tasks/ + Vault/Ops/Plans/ folders (filtered views, always in sync). Trigger: wrap-up, project-sync; on demand — "ops board" / "sync tasks". Hub: [[Ops/Dashboard — Ops|Dashboard — Ops]] · Per-project: [[Ops/Project Ops/Index|Project Ops Index]].

docs.title: Agent orientation
docs.text:
Authoritative state = each project note ## Status + live frontmatter on notes in Vault/Ops/Tasks/ and Vault/Ops/Plans/. Kanban columns are derived from that frontmatter — not the other way around.

Never parse .base files — they are Obsidian Bases views (filters over the same markdown cards). Agents read and write the .md card notes only.

Read order: hot.md is the fast session index (~500 words). Drill into the relevant project note ## Status when you need depth — not [[Home]]. Ops kanban cards supplement execution tracking; they do not replace Status.

Minimal bootstrap: repo CLAUDE.md → Vault/hot.md → Vault/CLAUDE.md → target project note ## Status (and Vault/Ops/Tasks/ only when doing ops work).

docs.title: Sync model (critical)
docs.text:
Layer Board file What it shows Roll-up tasks Vault/Ops/Bases/Work.base Open tasks in Tasks/ (+ Archive for shipped history) Roll-up plans Vault/Ops/Bases/Plans.base Open plans in Plans/ (+ Archive for shipped history) Per-project Vault/Ops/Bases/ByProject/{key}.base Same cards, filter project == "[[…]]"

Drag a card on Newfin Ops → Tasks and it moves on Work · Trello instantly — same file, same status frontmatter. No duplicate boards.

docs.title: Per-project hubs
docs.text:
Each project has its own .base file — Vault/Ops/Bases/ByProject/{key}.base — open in Obsidian as a native Bases tab (not markdown embed). Views:

View Type Trello Tasks kanban (primary — same as Tasks view) Plans Plans kanban Progress Done table

Linked from project vault notes (## Ops) and [[Ops/Project Ops/Index|Project Ops Index]]. Workspace Jackie Ops has a tab per project (Newfin · Tasks, Newfin · Plans, …).

Vault/Ops/Project Ops/{Name} Ops.md also embeds boards for reading in preview:

Board Folder Columns Tasks Tasks/ backlog → todo → doing → blocked (shipped → Archive/Tasks/) Plans Plans/ backlog → planned → active → deferred (shipped → Archive/Plans/) Progress table shipped cards in Archive/Tasks/ + Archive/Plans/ (sort by done date)

docs.title: Task schema (Vault/Ops/Tasks/)
docs.text:
title: Card title
kind: code | non-code
project: "[[Newfin]]"

docs.title: Plan schema (Vault/Ops/Plans/)
docs.text:
title: Plan title
kind: code | non-code

status: backlog       # NEW plans always backlog | planned | active | deferred | done
priority: 1

created: YYYY-MM-DD

Tasks vs plans: tasks = this week/session; plans = tracked initiative until done.

docs.title: Plan lifecycle (agents)
docs.text:
Event Action New row in future-improvements.md / roadmap / Projects/*/plans/ Create plan note → status: backlog, source: future-improvements or roadmap, set repo_plan Owner commits / promotes to dated plan in repo backlog → planned or active First task for plan moves to doing Plan → active if still backlog/planned Ship + catalog cleanup / roadmap reconcile Plan → done + done: <today>; remove matching backlog duplicate Deferred explicitly status: deferred

Do not create a task for every catalog line — plans hold ideas; tasks hold execution.

docs.text:
kind: code | non-code
lane: active | blocked | parked | dormant
next: one line
blocked:
ops_updated: YYYY-MM-DD

docs.title: Agent rules — project-sync (section F)
docs.text:
1. Set kind, next, blocked, ops_updated, lane from registry + latest Status.
  2. Do not edit Vault/Ops/Tasks/ or Vault/Ops/Plans/ in project-sync.

docs.title: Agent rules — wrap-up
docs.text:
Tasks

  1. Shipped work → matching doing task → done + done: date → move the card to Vault/Ops/Archive/Tasks/ (rename {project}-done-{slug}.md if not already).
  2. Stale doing → todo if pivoted.
  3. Status Next: / Projects/*/STATUS.md → new todo task if no open match.
  4. Blockers → blocked task or update existing.
  5. WIP ≤3 doing globally.

Plans

  1. On ship (roadmap reconcile): matching plan → done + done: → move to Vault/Ops/Archive/Plans/.
  2. On catalog pull: new Vault/Ops/Plans/ note per net-new future-improvements line → backlog.
  3. Promote backlog → active when execution starts.

Archive — shipped cards live in Vault/Ops/Archive/Tasks/ and Vault/Ops/Archive/Plans/; live folders hold only open work. Move on wrap-up, never delete.

Progress — derived view over Archive folders; never a third live folder.

When Vault/Ops/Bases/Work.base exists, morning-brief reads Vault/Ops/Tasks/ + Vault/Ops/Plans/ after project-sync — same cards as Obsidian kanban. Full contract: morning-brief § Ops board.

Quick flags: blocked task but lane: active · global doing >3 · active plan with zero open tasks.

docs.title: period-review
docs.text:
Purpose: the fractal review protocol — coach brief (Phase A) + coach session → Sergei note (Phase B) for week, month, and year closes. Monthly and yearly horizons live entirely in this file; weekly Phase A lives in weekly-review (scheduled, carries system steps). Trigger: monthly review / monthly coaching review / coaching review · yearly review (morning-brief nudges: month-end 📋; Jan 1–7 for prior year) · imported by weekly-review for Phase B. Role: Coach. Output: Vault/Briefs/…brief.md (Phase A) · Sergei period note at vault root (Phase B).

Folders: Jackie-OS (+ ~/dev/ when work/trading context matters).

docs.title: Gate — which phase runs
docs.text:
Check Action AI brief missing Run Phase A for that horizon (write brief, commit, stop) Brief exists, Sergei note missing Run Phase B below Both exist Report done; offer to append Sergei note section only if Sergei asks

Slugs + done signals: week YYYY-Www.md · month YYYY-Mmm.md (e.g. 2026-M06, not 2026-06) · year YYYY.md. Sergei note existing at vault root = done for morning-brief nudges.

docs.title: Phase A — Monthly brief
docs.text:
Read first: coaching, Vault/hot.md, [[About me]], [[Theses]], [[Coaching]], latest [[Self-portraits]]. Optional: latest psychological synthesis (pattern names only). Month window: previous calendar month unless stated in header.

Inputs (cap ~50 full bodies): dailies in month; Briefs/ daily briefs; Briefs/YYYY-Www brief.md overlapping weeks; [[Trading playbook]]; project Status + git since month start; prior Briefs/YYYY-Mmm brief.md for delta. Skip #private.

Write Vault/Briefs/YYYY-Mmm brief.md:

---
categories:
  - "[[Briefs]]"
  - "[[Coaching]]"
created: YYYY-MM-DD
month: YYYY-Mmm
---

# YYYY-Mmm — Monthly brief

*Coach's lens on [month]. Sergei owns the conclusions — evidence + questions, not diagnosis.*

Commit: Monthly brief YYYY-Mmm. Stop — tell Sergei: read [[YYYY-Mmm brief]], reply monthly review when ready. Persik: vault-only default (skip coo-push unless Sergei opts in).

docs.title: Phase A — Yearly brief

Read first: same stack as monthly. Inputs: all YYYY-Mmm / YYYY-Www briefs and Sergei notes in year; dailies (cap ~50); monthly briefs; [[Trading playbook]]; project Status arc. Skip #private.
